# POSCommander

POSCommander — двухпанельный файловый менеджер для Windows, вдохновлённый классическими файловыми менеджерами с двумя панелями.

## Возможности

- Две панели, вкладки, навигация по дискам и папкам.
- Копирование, перемещение, удаление и переименование файлов и папок.
- Перетаскивание между панелями: по умолчанию перемещение на том же диске и копирование между дисками; удерживайте __Ctrl__, чтобы копировать.
- Контекстное меню с просмотром, копированием, перемещением, переименованием, удалением и системным окном свойств Windows.
- Работа с ZIP, 7z и другими поддерживаемыми 7-Zip форматами: просмотр содержимого, создание и извлечение архивов.
- Поиск файлов, командная строка с автодополнением и историей.
- Просмотр файлов и отображение системных значков Windows.

## Установка

Скачайте `POSCommander-Setup-<версия>.exe` со страницы Releases, запустите установщик и выберите папку установки. Установщик создаёт ярлыки в меню «Пуск» и на рабочем столе.

## Разработка

Требуются Windows, Node.js и npm.

```
npm install
npm start
```

Сборка приложения и установщика:

```
npm run build
npm run build:exe
```

`npm run build:exe` создаёт папку `release/build-<дата-времени>/` с распакованным приложением (`win-unpacked/POSCommander.exe`) и полным установщиком NSIS (`POSCommander-Setup-<версия>.exe`). Установщик позволяет выбрать каталог и создаёт ярлыки.

## Основные клавиши

| Клавиша | Действие |
| --- | --- |
| `F3` | Просмотр файла |
| `F4` | Правка файла |
| `F5` | Копирование |
| `F6` | Перемещение |
| `Shift+F6` | Переименование |
| `F7` | Создание папки |
| `F8` | Удаление |
| `Tab` | Переключение между панелями |
| `Ctrl+↑` / `Ctrl+↓` | История командной строки |

В окнах подтверждения стрелки перемещают фокус между кнопками; `Enter` активирует выбранную кнопку, `Esc` закрывает окно или отменяет действие.

## Технологии

Electron, TypeScript, HTML и CSS. Архивы обрабатываются встроенным 7-Zip (`7zip-bin`).

## Лицензия

MIT. См. LICENSE.

Файловый менеджер в духе Total Commander: две панели, клавиатура-first,
вкладки, командная строка, панель функциональных клавиш.

**Стек:** C# / .NET 10 + Avalonia UI · Windows-first, ядро кроссплатформенное.

План и вехи: [docs/PLAN.md](docs/PLAN.md)

## Установка

`POSCommanderSetup-0.1.0.exe` — установка без прав администратора (в профиль
пользователя), ярлык в меню «Пуск», удаление через «Приложения».

Портативный вариант: `POSCommander.App.exe` — один файл, ничего не требует.

## Что уже работает

| Блок | Состояние |
|---|---|
| Две панели, диски, вкладки, фильтр масок | готово |
| Колонки Имя / Тип / Размер / Дата: сортировка по клику, ширина — перетаскиванием границы | готово |
| Меню, панель инструментов, средняя панель, F-клавиши | готово |
| Командная строка (переход по пути, запуск команд) | готово |
| F3 просмотр (текст до 512 КБ), F4 правка во внешнем редакторе | готово |
| F5 копирование, F6 перемещение | прогресс, пауза, отмена, конфликты (заменить/пропустить/оба/новее/старше), ошибки по файлам |
| F7 каталог, Delete — корзина, Shift+Delete — безвозвратно | готово |
| Shift+F6 переименование, Alt+Enter свойства | готово |
| Поиск файлов (Alt+F7): маска, текст, размер, подкаталоги | готово |
| Архивы zip как папки: вход по Enter, распаковка F5, упаковка Alt+F5 | готово (только zip) |
| Иконки оболочки Windows в списке файлов | готово |
| 7z/rar, FTP/SFTP, плагины | не начаты (M4–M6) |

# POSCommander — архитектурный план

Статус: черновик v0.1 · дата: 2026-11-04

Цель: файловый менеджер с функциональным паритетом Total Commander —
клавиатура-first, две панели, всё через очередь операций, расширяемый плагинами.

---

## 0. Принятые решения (ADR)

| ID | Решение | Обоснование |
|---|---|---|
| ADR-001 | **C# / .NET 10 + Avalonia UI** | 70% работы — интеграция с ОС, 30% — UI. BCL + NuGet закрывают ФС, архивы, FTP/SFTP, SSH. Avalonia даёт виртуализированные списки и одну кодовую базу на 3 ОС. |
| ADR-002 | **Windows-first, ядро кроссплатформенное** | Windows-специфика (ACL, корзина, shell-меню, `\\?\`) идёт через `IPlatform*`-абстракции, а не в ядро. Linux/macOS добавляются без переписывания. |
| ADR-003 | **Свой плагинный API, мост к TC-плагинам — позже** | Совместимость с `.wcx/.wfx` — это C ABI, 32/64-бит и годы работы. Сначала стабильное ядро и свой managed API. |
| ADR-004 | **Ядро без ссылок на UI** | Тесты, CLI-режим, будущий серверный вариант — бесплатно. Нарушение этого правила считается дефектом архитектуры. |
| ADR-005 | **Свой движок операций, не `File.Copy`** | Нужны пауза, докачка, лимит скорости, конфликты по файлу, сохранение метаданных, длинные пути. |
| ADR-006 | **MVVM + code-behind только для рендера списка** | Панель — самый горячий путь UI, там допустим ручной рендер; всё остальное — MVVM. |

---

## 1. Что значит «паритет»: критерии приёмки по группам

| # | Группа | Критерий «готово» |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Две панели | 100 000 записей листаются без залипания; курсор и выделение не теряются при обновлении; natural sort; вкладки; история; закладки; быстрый фильтр; плоский вид; полный keymap |
| 2 | Операции | Копирование 20 ГБ: пауза/продолжить/отмена, лимит скорости, 5 политик конфликта, ошибка на файле не убивает операцию, сохранение mtime/атрибутов/ACL/ADS, пути > 260 символов |
| 3 | Просмотр/правка | Lister: текст (кодировки, wrap, hex), изображения, медиа; сравнение по содержимому (текст/бинарь); внутренний редактор с подсветкой |
| 4 | Поиск | Маски, regex, содержимое, даты, размеры, поиск внутри архивов, сохранённые шаблоны, «найти всё» |

$exe='E:\Work\VSC\POSCommander\artifacts\publish\POSCommander.App.exe'
function Measure-App($path,$name){
  $sw=[Diagnostics.Stopwatch]::StartNew()
  $p=Start-Process $path -PassThru
  while(-not $p.HasExited -and $p.MainWindowHandle -eq 0 -and $sw.ElapsedMilliseconds -lt 20000){ Start-Sleep -Milliseconds 20; $p.Refresh() }
  $t=$sw.ElapsedMilliseconds
  Start-Sleep 4; $p.Refresh()
  $procs = Get-Process | Where-Object { $_.Id -eq $p.Id -or ($_.Parent -and $_.Parent.Id -eq $p.Id) }
  $ws = ($procs | Measure-Object WorkingSet64 -Sum).Sum/1MB
  $pv = ($procs | Measure-Object PrivateMemorySize64 -Sum).Sum/1MB
  '{0}: окно через {1} мс, WorkingSet {2:N0} МБ, Private {3:N0} МБ, процессов {4}' -f $name,$t,$ws,$pv,$procs.Count
  taskkill /T /F /PID $p.Id | Out-Null
}

data.text:
I'm noting that the Electron build isn't set up here, and that a typical Electron app would run to roughly 150–300 MB across several processes with a launch time of 1–2 seconds, so there's no need to install it. Total Commander, by contrast, uses about 32 MB of working set and is a native Win32 app written in Delphi/Lazarus. For the recommendation, I'm weighing options for maximum speed, low memory, and fast startup that still feel like TC, starting with C++ on the Win32 API or WTL using a native ListView in virtual mode with LVS_OWNERDATA. TC itself is written in Delphi, so...

Among the native options, Delphi or Lazarus is worth a look since that's what Total Commander itself is built with, and Double Commander is an open-source Lazarus clone I could study. C# WinForms on .NET Framework 4.8 or .NET 10 with ReadyToRun could keep the existing C# core, though it would be heavier at roughly 30-70 MB and 300-500 ms to start. Writing raw Win32 from C# with CsWin32 and NativeAOT might reach about 100 ms and 15-25 MB, but it feels clunky.

I'm weighing the native-control options against the C# route, since matching Total Commander's look comes almost for free with Win32 widgets. Lazarus/Free Pascal stands out as the same stack TC uses, and Double Commander is a usable reference, though its GPL license would clash with the repo's MIT terms if I forked it.

I'm settling on C++20 with the pure Win32 API, optionally with WTL, built with MSVC and CMake so it works from VS Code, and using a virtual ListView for the file panels. Rust and Lazarus are plausible too, but the C++ Win32 route has the most reference material and fits how this project is being developed.

I'm now weighing how the C++ route would handle the file panels and system pieces: IFileOperation or CopyFileEx for copying, the shell context menu, system image list icons, and archive access through 7z.dll. The main argument for it is that Total Commander's WCX and WLX plugins use a C ABI, so a native C++ build could load them directly, which would make functional parity much more realistic than in a managed rewrite.

I'm weighing whether to measure the C# option more, but I only have the .NET 8 runtime here with no SDK, so I can't build anything and will have to present those numbers as estimates. Avalonia's current measurements look like a 49 MB single-file exe and a 1.4 to 2.7 second start to window, with about 170 MB of working set, against Total Commander's 32 MB; that comparison is rough because TC was a long-running instance with its folders loaded.

Now I'm looking at the real bottlenecks in the Electron code: directory listing stats each file one at a time, drive detection shells out to PowerShell, and rendering rebuilds every row without virtualization. A Win32 version would sidestep most of that, since FindFirstFileEx returns size and timestamps in one pass. Next I'm thinking about wrapping up with a short offer to scaffold the project, probably in Russian.

Next I'm planning the migration in phases: first the window, the two virtual listviews, drives, tabs, F-keys and the command line, then file operations through IFileOperation or CopyFileEx, and later 7z.dll plus WCX and WLX plugins. Much of the existing docs and keymap carries over, though the code itself won't port.

Я посмотрел обе ваши версии: Electron на GitHub (TypeScript, около 3,8 тыс. строк) и текущую на C# / .NET 10 + Avalonia 12 в `E:\Work\VSC\POSCommander` (около 5,2 тыс. строк, v0.1.7). Ваше подозрение верное: для таких целей оба стека не подходят.

## Замеры на вашей машине

| | Запуск до окна | ОЗУ (Working Set / Private) | Размер exe |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Total Commander** (запущен у вас, E:\Distr\TCPU68) | — | **32 / 11 МБ** | ~5 МБ |
| **POSCommander на Avalonia** (`artifacts\publish`) | **1,4 с** при повторном запуске, **2,7 с** при первом | **170 / 150 МБ** | **49 МБ** |
| POSCommander на Electron | не замерял, сборки на диске нет | обычно 150–300 МБ на 4+ процесса | ~150 МБ+ |

Avalonia расходует памяти примерно в 5–13 раз больше, чем TC, и запускается в 10–20 раз медленнее. Причина в архитектуре, оптимизацией её не убрать: в процессе живут среда .NET, Skia (движок, который сам рисует весь интерфейс) и XAML.

## Почему так получается

- **Electron** держит внутри целый браузер. В коде есть и свои узкие места: для каждого файла отдельный запрос информации по очереди (`fsservice.ts`), список дисков берётся через PowerShell (около секунды на вызов), весь список строк перерисовывается целиком.
- **Avalonia** рисует интерфейс сама, а не стандартными элементами Windows. Поэтому список, заголовки колонок, меню и вкладки только «похожи» на TC, и каждую деталь приходится подгонять вручную (у вас уже несколько коммитов вида «как в TC»).
- **Total Commander** собран на Delphi, 64-битная версия — на Lazarus. Он использует **родные элементы Windows**, поэтому быстрый и выглядит именно так.

## Что рекомендую: C++ и чистый Win32 API (MSVC + CMake, работает в VS Code)

1. **Внешний вид TC получается сам.** На вашем скриншоте почти всё — стандартные элементы Windows: меню, панель инструментов, вкладки, таблица файлов с заголовками колонок, строка состояния, командная строка, кнопки F3–F8. Подгонять их стилями не нужно.
2. **Скорость.** Ожидаемо (это оценка, не замер): запуск за 50–150 мс, память 10–25 МБ, exe 1–3 МБ без установщика среды выполнения.
   - Список рисует только видимые строки, поэтому 100 000 файлов не тормозят.
   - Чтение папки одним проходом сразу отдаёт размер и дату, без отдельного запроса на каждый файл.
   - Иконки берутся из общего системного кэша Windows.
3. **Функции TC делаются системными средствами.** Есть родное контекстное меню Проводника, копирование с прогрессом и паузой, корзина, свойства без PowerShell. Архивы 7z/rar/zip открываются напрямую через 7z.dll.
4. **Главное — плагины TC.** Форматы плагинов (wcx — архивы, wfx — файловые системы, wlx — просмотр, wdx — колонки) рассчитаны на программы на C. В C++ их можно подключать напрямую и сразу получить готовые плагины: FTP/SFTP, просмотрщики, архиваторы. В вашем PLAN.md (ADR-003) это отложено как «годы работы» — для C++ это обычная задача.

## Альтернативы

| Вариант | Плюсы | Минусы |
|---|---|---|
| **Lazarus / Free Pascal** | Тот же стек, что у TC x64. Есть Double Commander — открытый клон TC, можно подсматривать | Лицензия GPL (у вас MIT). Слабая поддержка в VS Code |
| **Rust + Win32** (`windows-rs`) | Скорость как у C++, безопасность памяти | Много шаблонного кода, мало примеров GUI на Win32 |
| **Оставить C#, заменить UI на WinForms** | Можно сохранить Core и тесты | Ожидаемо 40–70 МБ и 0,3–0,6 с — лучше Avalonia, но далеко от TC |

## Что можно взять из текущего проекта

Код в новый стек не перенести. Но пригодятся критерии приёмки из `docs/PLAN.md`, раскладка клавиш, логика конфликтов при копировании (заменить / пропустить / новее…) и список сценариев для тестов.

Могу создать новый проект в `POSCommander2`: окно с двумя панелями, диски, вкладки, командная строка, кнопки F-клавиш и навигация. Для сборки нужен MSVC — Visual Studio Build Tools. Сейчас в окружении есть только среда .NET 8 без SDK, поэтому собрать здесь я ничего не смогу, пока Build Tools не установлены.

1. **Внешний вид TC получается сам.** На вашем скриншоте почти всё — стандартные элементы Windows: меню, панель инструментов, вкладки, таблица файлов с заголовками колонок, строка состояния, командная строка, кнопки F3–F8. Подгонять их стилями не нужно.
2. **Скорость.** Ожидаемо (это оценка, не замер): запуск за 50–150 мс, память 10–25 МБ, exe 1–3 МБ без установщика среды выполнения.
   - Список рисует только видимые строки, поэтому 100 000 файлов не тормозят.
   - Чтение папки одним проходом сразу отдаёт размер и дату, без отдельного запроса на каждый файл.
   - Иконки берутся из общего системного кэша Windows.
3. **Функции TC делаются системными средствами.** Есть родное контекстное меню Проводника, копирование с прогрессом и паузой, корзина, свойства без PowerShell. Архивы 7z/rar/zip открываются напрямую через 7z.dll.
4. **Главное — плагины TC.** Форматы плагинов (wcx — архивы, wfx — файловые системы, wlx — просмотр, wdx — колонки) рассчитаны на программы на C. В C++ их можно подключать напрямую и сразу получить готовые плагины: FTP/SFTP, просмотрщики, архиваторы. В вашем PLAN.md (ADR-003) это отложено как «годы работы» — для C++ это обычная задача.

## Альтернативы

| Вариант | Плюсы | Минусы |
|---|---|---|
| **Lazarus / Free Pascal** | Тот же стек, что у TC x64. Есть Double Commander — открытый клон TC, можно подсматривать | Лицензия GPL (у вас MIT). Слабая поддержка в VS Code |
| **Rust + Win32** (`windows-rs`) | Скорость как у C++, безопасность памяти | Много шаблонного кода, мало примеров GUI на Win32 |
| **Оставить C#, заменить UI на WinForms** | Можно сохранить Core и тесты | Ожидаемо 40–70 МБ и 0,3–0,6 с — лучше Avalonia, но далеко от TC |

## Что можно взять из текущего проекта

Код в новый стек не перенести. Но пригодятся критерии приёмки из `docs/PLAN.md`, раскладка клавиш, логика конфликтов при копировании (заменить / пропустить / новее…) и список сценариев для тестов.

Могу создать новый проект в `POSCommander2`: окно с двумя панелями, диски, вкладки, командная строка, кнопки F-клавиш и навигация. Для сборки нужен MSVC — Visual Studio Build Tools. Сейчас в окружении есть только среда .NET 8 без SDK, поэтому собрать здесь я ничего не смогу, пока Build Tools не установлены.

data.text:
I've confirmed there's no MSVC here, but w64devkit's MinGW g++ and cmake and ninja are available, so I can build with MinGW now. I'll write the CMake to support both MSVC and MinGW, then check the compiler versions.

I'm weighing whether to pause and propose a plan first, but since the user already asked for the project outright, I'll just move forward with a todo checklist. The MVP scope is a main window with menus, toolbar, drive bars, tabs, path header, a virtual report-mode list, and a command line, plus keyboard navigation and F-key actions.

I'm laying out the rest of the MVP: F5 and F6 through IFileOperation, F7 for making folders, F8 and Delete sending files to the recycle bin, Shift+F6 for in-place rename, and Alt+F4 to exit. I'm also considering a native shell context menu, saving the paths and window position to an INI file, and showing free-space and selection counts in the status lines, with Ctrl+R for refresh instead of automatic directory watching.

Next I'm sketching the project layout: a CMakeLists.txt and presets for MinGW and MSVC, plus a main entry point, a main window module, and a panel module that handles drives, tabs, and the file list.

Next I'm listing the remaining modules: a file-system helper for listing, sorting, and formatting, a shell-operations module for IFileOperation, the context menu, and properties, plus a simple input dialog. I'll also add a manifest for common controls and high-DPI, and project files for VS Code and the docs.

I'm adding the .gitignore, .editorconfig, and an MIT license, then a PowerShell script to benchmark startup time and memory. Next I'm working out keyboard handling: the list view is the focus control, so key messages get intercepted before dispatch, and printable characters are forwarded into the command line while focus stays in the panel.

I'm working out how to handle keyboard input in the file list: printable characters go into the command line, Backspace edits it, and Esc clears it, matching Total Commander. For the list itself I'm using a virtual list view, with a separate per-item selected flag drawn in red, while the cursor stays on the focused item.

I'm setting the list up with single selection so the cursor bar stays, and drawing marked files in red through custom draw. Insert toggles a mark and moves down, Ctrl+click toggles marks, and Num+/Num-/Num*/Ctrl+A handle selection by mask or all at once. I'm also about to pull the system icons through SHGetFileInfo.

I'm figuring out how to get the system icons: SHGetFileInfo with the system image list, and sharing that list with the ListView. Extension-based lookups skip disk access, but .exe, .lnk, and similar files need their real path, so I'll fetch those lazily for visible items only and cache the results.

I'm settling on the sorting rules: ".." stays at the top, directories always come first sorted by name, and files follow the chosen column. I'm also planning natural-order comparison for the names.

I'm settling how file names and sizes get displayed: names get split at the extension into their own column, except for dotfiles like ".gitignore" that keep the whole name, and sizes follow Total Commander's format with units and "<Папка>" for folders.

I'm figuring out the status line and the drive bar now. The status line will show the selected size and the file and folder counts, and the drive bar will be a toolbar with a small icon and letter for each drive.

I'm working out the tab labels and the path header now: tabs show "drive:foldername" (just "drive:" for a root), and the path header will show the current path in a box that turns blue when that panel is active.

I'm settling on the header colors now: the active panel's path header should be a light blue, and I'm weighing whether to use a fixed RGB value or a system color instead.

I'm settling on the header colors: the active panel's path header will use the system active-caption color with black text, and the inactive one will use the inactive-caption color, which matches how Total Commander looks. I'm also thinking about adding history back and forward through Alt+Left and Alt+Right, and maybe a dropdown later, and I'm starting on the command line row, which pairs a path label with an edit box.

I'm looking at how the command line should run what the user types: a first pass that tries ShellExecuteExW on the first token with the rest as parameters, and a fallback through cmd if that fails. I'm also planning the F-key bar row next.

I'm setting up the toolbar with standard system icons for actions like refresh, new tab, copy, move, delete, properties, and create, leaving out find for now.

Now I'm laying out the menu bar in the resource file, starting with the File menu for opening, viewing, editing, copying, moving, creating folders, deleting, properties, and exit, and I'm about to fill in the Selection menu.

I'm settling the Commands menu now: refresh on Ctrl+R, switching drives, jumping to the root, opening a command line, and swapping panels with Ctrl+U. The View menu will hold the sort options, by name, extension, date, size, or none, each with its Ctrl+F shortcut.

I'm setting up the menus next: the Commands menu gets a Ctrl+T-style tab group, a close, and next and previous tab shortcuts, plus a drive-selection popup on Alt+F1 and Alt+F2 for each panel. Ctrl+PgUp goes up a directory, Ctrl+\ jumps to the root, and Alt+Left/Right handle history. For Ctrl+Left/Right, I'm making it open the folder under the cursor in the other panel, or the current one if the cursor isn't on a folder.

I'm settling on Shift+F6 as in-place rename, but the ListView label edit shows only the name without its extension, while Total Commander edits the full name, so the split columns will need some handling for that.

I'm planning the F3 viewer as a minimal read-only text lister: a multiline EDIT that loads the file, detects UTF-8, UTF-16, or ANSI (1251), and closes on Esc.

I'm settling the F4 editor to open the file in Notepad, or whatever editor the ini names. For F5 and F6 I'm planning an input dialog prefilled with the other panel's path, then copying through IFileOperation into that folder, or renaming for a single file if the target isn't an existing directory.

I'm settling the confirm-and-delete flow next: F8 and Del ask before sending the selection to the Recycle Bin through IFileOperation, while Shift+F8 and Shift+Del delete permanently. After any operation I'll refresh both panels.

I'm planning to refresh the panels when files change on disk, using a change-notification handle per panel that the message loop waits on, with a short debounce before reloading. After a reload I'll restore the cursor to the same file and keep the marked selection, and I'll load directories synchronously with FindFirstFileExW.

I'm settling on hidden files: the default will show them, with a toggle under the View menu on Ctrl+H. For quick search, I'm weighing Alt+letter, since it collides with menu accelerators, so I'll need to pick something else.

I'm laying out the panel stack now: a drive bar, a tab strip, the path header, the file list, and a status line, with a draggable splitter between the two panels. I'm also planning for high DPI by scaling the layout with the window's DPI and using the system message font.

I'm checking the font and DPI handling next: scaling the UI with the window's DPI, and using the Windows message font since Total Commander uses a similar system font. I'm also thinking about where the settings file should live, either in the app data folder or next to the executable for a portable setup.

I'm settling the settings file: it goes next to the exe as poscmd.ini if one is already there, otherwise under %APPDATA%\POSCommander. I'll save the window placement, splitter ratio, active panel, tabs, sort settings, and the hidden-files toggle, and I'll create the file with a UTF-16LE BOM first so Unicode paths survive.

I'm checking the toolchain next, the g++ version and whether the IFileOperation and GetDpiForWindow headers are available. For the build I'll use static linking and wWinMain with the GUI subsystem, linking against comctl32, shell32, shlwapi, ole32, uuid, gdi32, user32, and uxtheme. I'm also weighing whether the ListView should use the Explorer theme, which gives a light blue selection rather than the dark blue full-row bar Total Commander uses.

I'm settling the listview's look: the cursor row and the header's sort arrow will use the standard system highlight and HDF_SORTUP/DOWN flags, with marked files drawn in red through custom draw.

I'm weighing the cursor row in the listview now. I can't just drop the system selection, since comctl ignores custom text colors on selected items. So the plan is to strip the selected state in custom draw for the cursor row and paint its background and text myself, keeping marked files red.

I'm settling the cursor row now: the cursor will be drawn through custom draw using only the focus state, so the system selection highlight gets stripped. The active panel will show the highlight color, while the inactive panel will just get a dotted focus frame.

I'm working out the cursor colour now: the active panel's cursor row gets a light blue fill, and I'm still choosing the exact RGB value to match Total Commander's look.

I'm settling the cursor colour as a light blue, roughly RGB(204,232,255) with black text, to match the screenshot, and I'll keep it in a Theme struct so it can become configurable later. For the row height I'm going with the default ListView metrics at Segoe UI 9, which should land around 17 to 20 pixels per row, and I'm now sizing the columns.

I'm working out how Enter, Backspace and double-click should open things, with the cursor landing back on the folder I came from when going up. For drives I'm planning an Alt+F1/F2 popup, and each panel will remember the last path used on each drive.

I'm planning the drive icons through stock system icons per drive type, so network and removable drives don't need a disk access to get their icon. Next I'll look at how to get the free space label for each drive.

I'm working out the free-space label for each drive, and I'll format the sizes with a comma decimal and spaces for thousands. The status line will show the selected size and the file and folder counts, and I'm planning to refresh the drive bars on device changes. Each tab will keep its own path, history, and sort settings.

I'm settling the tab keys next: Ctrl+T will duplicate the current tab, Ctrl+W will close it as long as more than one is open, and Ctrl+Tab will move to the next one. I'm skipping double-click-to-close on tabs since that needs subclassing, so the menu and Ctrl+W will cover it. I'm also planning the main loop around MsgWaitForMultipleObjects, so the directory watch handles get serviced alongside window messages.

I'm wiring up the message loop so it pulls each message through a PreTranslate hook first, and only falls back to the normal translate-and-dispatch path when that hook doesn't claim it. Key handling will apply to the whole main window except the command-line edit and label editing: F-keys work everywhere, while Enter, Esc, Tab, and Up/Down in the command line get their own handling.

I'm handling typed characters from the file list: when a printable key reaches the listview, I'll forward it to the command-line edit and swallow it, so ListView's incremental search never kicks in. The letter keydown still passes through so that WM_CHAR gets generated for it.

I'm settling the space and Enter behavior: when the command line has text, space types into it and Enter runs the command, otherwise space marks the file and Enter opens the item. Backspace will go to the command-line edit as a character when it has text, so it deletes there.

I'm mapping out the keyboard handling for the active listview: Tab switches panels, Ctrl+Tab moves between tabs, and Enter either runs the command line or opens the selected item. For the command-line edit, I'll position the caret at the end before forwarding characters, so typed text and Backspace land where expected.

I'm going through the remaining keys: Ctrl+Shift+Enter would put the full path in the command line, and Alt+Enter opens properties. Backspace goes up a directory, and Insert marks the file and moves down. I'm still deciding whether Space should move the cursor down, since Total Commander's default behavior is unclear to me here.

I'm working through the Space and Insert keys now: both mark the file and move the cursor down, and for directories Space should trigger a size calculation on a background thread that updates the Size column. I'm also planning mask-based select, deselect, and invert on the numpad keys.

I'm listing the remaining function keys: F3 through F8 with their Shift and Alt variants, plus Del and Shift+Del, and I'm leaving search and the Ctrl+Num- chord for later.

I'm listing the rest of the keyboard map now: Alt+Left/Right for history, Ctrl+U to swap panels, Ctrl+Left/Right to open in the other panel, Ctrl+F3 through F7 for sorting, and Ctrl+H for hidden files. I'll leave bookmarks and quick view for later, and Shift+F10 or the context-menu key will open a shell menu at the cursor.

I'm going through the remaining clipboard shortcuts: Ctrl+C and Ctrl+X will put the selected files on the clipboard as a file drop, and Ctrl+V will paste them into the current directory with a copy or move depending on the drop effect. I'm leaving drag and drop for a later milestone.

I'm wiring the context menu through the shell: I'll get an IShellFolder for the directory, bind each selected item to a child pidl, and ask for its IContextMenu. Then I'll build the popup, track it at the cursor, and invoke whatever command comes back, forwarding messages to IContextMenu2/3 for submenus.

I'm settling how Alt+Enter opens properties: I'll use the context menu's "properties" verb for every selection, so single and multiple items behave the same way. The properties dialog runs on its own thread inside the process, so I need to make sure messages keep flowing while it's open.

I'm working out how to call IFileOperation for copy and move: I'll create the operation object, set the owner window and flags, then queue a CopyItem for each source path with its target name and run PerformOperations. The UI thread will handle it, and I'll check whether the operation was aborted.

I'm settling how the file operations run: IFileOperation will block while its own progress dialog pumps messages, which is acceptable for the MVP even though a real background queue is a later roadmap item. For delete, I'll use the recycle flag on Windows 8 and later, and for permanent delete I'll skip the undo flag so it's gone for good.

I'm setting up the lister window as a read-only multiline edit with a monospace font, closing it on Esc, and capping file reads at 32 MB with a truncation note in the title. I'll detect the encoding from the BOM, falling back to UTF-8 if it validates and to the system ANSI code page otherwise.

I'm settling the lister and input dialogs now: the lister is a read-only multiline edit that reads up to a size cap and converts line endings for display, and the input dialog is a generic prompt-and-edit box I'll reuse for copy and other prompts. I'll also confirm deletes with a localized yes/no message and show the about box as a simple message box.

I'm laying out the settings save, the splitter between the two panels, and which panel is active, with each panel's child controls parented directly to the main window so notifications arrive there.

I'm setting up the toolbar drive buttons with text and images, using the system small image list, which the toolbar won't destroy on its own.

I'm settling the layout details: the toolbar's own height sets the drive bar, and the rest of the panel stacks around it at DPI-scaled sizes. The system small image list is fine to share since neither the toolbar nor the listview will destroy it. For the header and status labels, I just need to handle the static control colors and keep the status text plain.

I'm sizing the layout rows now: the drive bar takes the toolbar's button height plus a little padding, and the tab row follows the first tab item's bottom edge. The header and status labels each get the text height plus a small margin, and the command-line row will use the combo box's height once it's created.

I'm setting the font height aside and turning to the main toolbar: it'll load the standard, view, and history bitmaps, and I'm sketching out the button list, including back, forward, and favorites.

Continuing the toolbar setup, I'm listing the standard, view, and history image indices I want for the main buttons, covering the usual clipboard, undo, delete, file, print, find and sort icons along with the parent-folder, network and new-folder ones.

Now I'm laying out the main toolbar buttons: back, forward, and up on the first group, then copy, cut, and paste, followed by new folder, delete, and properties. Sort buttons for name, type, size, and date come next, then a new-tab button and a console button using the file-open icon.

I'm skipping a dedicated console button in the toolbar, since that action already lives in the Commands menu as "Open console" and opens cmd.exe in the current directory. For tooltips, I'll let the toolbar send TTN_GETDISPINFO to the main window keyed by command id and return the text there. I'm keeping the 16px icons even at high DPI, since they're small but workable, and then I'll check the toolchain.

I'm laying out the panel stack now: a drive bar, a tab strip, the path header, the file list, and a status line, with a draggable splitter between the two panels. I'm also planning for high DPI by scaling the layout with the window's DPI and using the system message font.

I'm checking the font and DPI handling next: scaling the UI with the window's DPI, and using the Windows message font since Total Commander uses a similar system font. I'm also thinking about where the settings file should live, either in the app data folder or next to the executable for a portable setup.

I'm settling the settings file: it goes next to the exe as poscmd.ini if one is already there, otherwise under %APPDATA%\POSCommander. I'll save the window placement, splitter ratio, active panel, tabs, sort settings, and the hidden-files toggle, and I'll create the file with a UTF-16LE BOM first so Unicode paths survive.

I'm checking the toolchain next, the g++ version and whether the IFileOperation and GetDpiForWindow headers are available. For the build I'll use static linking and wWinMain with the GUI subsystem, linking against comctl32, shell32, shlwapi, ole32, uuid, gdi32, user32, and uxtheme. I'm also weighing whether the ListView should use the Explorer theme, which gives a light blue selection rather than the dark blue full-row bar Total Commander uses.

I'm settling the listview's look: the cursor row and the header's sort arrow will use the standard system highlight and HDF_SORTUP/DOWN flags, with marked files drawn in red through custom draw.

I'm weighing the cursor row in the listview now. I can't just drop the system selection, since comctl ignores custom text colors on selected items. So the plan is to strip the selected state in custom draw for the cursor row and paint its background and text myself, keeping marked files red.

I'm settling the cursor row now: the cursor will be drawn through custom draw using only the focus state, so the system selection highlight gets stripped. The active panel will show the highlight color, while the inactive panel will just get a dotted focus frame.

I'm working out the cursor colour now: the active panel's cursor row gets a light blue fill, and I'm still choosing the exact RGB value to match Total Commander's look.

I'm settling the cursor colour as a light blue, roughly RGB(204,232,255) with black text, to match the screenshot, and I'll keep it in a Theme struct so it can become configurable later. For the row height I'm going with the default ListView metrics at Segoe UI 9, which should land around 17 to 20 pixels per row, and I'm now sizing the columns.

I'm working out how Enter, Backspace and double-click should open things, with the cursor landing back on the folder I came from when going up. For drives I'm planning an Alt+F1/F2 popup, and each panel will remember the last path used on each drive.

I'm planning the drive icons through stock system icons per drive type, so network and removable drives don't need a disk access to get their icon. Next I'll look at how to get the free space label for each drive.

I'm working out the free-space label for each drive, and I'll format the sizes with a comma decimal and spaces for thousands. The status line will show the selected size and the file and folder counts, and I'm planning to refresh the drive bars on device changes. Each tab will keep its own path, history, and sort settings.

I'm settling the tab keys next: Ctrl+T will duplicate the current tab, Ctrl+W will close it as long as more than one is open, and Ctrl+Tab will move to the next one. I'm skipping double-click-to-close on tabs since that needs subclassing, so the menu and Ctrl+W will cover it. I'm also planning the main loop around MsgWaitForMultipleObjects, so the directory watch handles get serviced alongside window messages.

I'm wiring up the message loop so it pulls each message through a PreTranslate hook first, and only falls back to the normal translate-and-dispatch path when that hook doesn't claim it. Key handling will apply to the whole main window except the command-line edit and label editing: F-keys work everywhere, while Enter, Esc, Tab, and Up/Down in the command line get their own handling.

I'm handling typed characters from the file list: when a printable key reaches the listview, I'll forward it to the command-line edit and swallow it, so ListView's incremental search never kicks in. The letter keydown still passes through so that WM_CHAR gets generated for it.

I'm settling the space and Enter behavior: when the command line has text, space types into it and Enter runs the command, otherwise space marks the file and Enter opens the item. Backspace will go to the command-line edit as a character when it has text, so it deletes there.

I'm mapping out the keyboard handling for the active listview: Tab switches panels, Ctrl+Tab moves between tabs, and Enter either runs the command line or opens the selected item. For the command-line edit, I'll position the caret at the end before forwarding characters, so typed text and Backspace land where expected.

I'm going through the remaining keys: Ctrl+Shift+Enter would put the full path in the command line, and Alt+Enter opens properties. Backspace goes up a directory, and Insert marks the file and moves down. I'm still deciding whether Space should move the cursor down, since Total Commander's default behavior is unclear to me here.

I'm working through the Space and Insert keys now: both mark the file and move the cursor down, and for directories Space should trigger a size calculation on a background thread that updates the Size column. I'm also planning mask-based select, deselect, and invert on the numpad keys.

I'm listing the remaining function keys: F3 through F8 with their Shift and Alt variants, plus Del and Shift+Del, and I'm leaving search and the Ctrl+Num- chord for later.

I'm listing the rest of the keyboard map now: Alt+Left/Right for history, Ctrl+U to swap panels, Ctrl+Left/Right to open in the other panel, Ctrl+F3 through F7 for sorting, and Ctrl+H for hidden files. I'll leave bookmarks and quick view for later, and Shift+F10 or the context-menu key will open a shell menu at the cursor.

I'm going through the remaining clipboard shortcuts: Ctrl+C and Ctrl+X will put the selected files on the clipboard as a file drop, and Ctrl+V will paste them into the current directory with a copy or move depending on the drop effect. I'm leaving drag and drop for a later milestone.

I'm wiring the context menu through the shell: I'll get an IShellFolder for the directory, bind each selected item to a child pidl, and ask for its IContextMenu. Then I'll build the popup, track it at the cursor, and invoke whatever command comes back, forwarding messages to IContextMenu2/3 for submenus.

I'm settling how Alt+Enter opens properties: I'll use the context menu's "properties" verb for every selection, so single and multiple items behave the same way. The properties dialog runs on its own thread inside the process, so I need to make sure messages keep flowing while it's open.

I'm working out how to call IFileOperation for copy and move: I'll create the operation object, set the owner window and flags, then queue a CopyItem for each source path with its target name and run PerformOperations. The UI thread will handle it, and I'll check whether the operation was aborted.

I'm settling how the file operations run: IFileOperation will block while its own progress dialog pumps messages, which is acceptable for the MVP even though a real background queue is a later roadmap item. For delete, I'll use the recycle flag on Windows 8 and later, and for permanent delete I'll skip the undo flag so it's gone for good.

I'm setting up the lister window as a read-only multiline edit with a monospace font, closing it on Esc, and capping file reads at 32 MB with a truncation note in the title. I'll detect the encoding from the BOM, falling back to UTF-8 if it validates and to the system ANSI code page otherwise.

I'm settling the lister and input dialogs now: the lister is a read-only multiline edit that reads up to a size cap and converts line endings for display, and the input dialog is a generic prompt-and-edit box I'll reuse for copy and other prompts. I'll also confirm deletes with a localized yes/no message and show the about box as a simple message box.

I'm laying out the settings save, the splitter between the two panels, and which panel is active, with each panel's child controls parented directly to the main window so notifications arrive there.

I'm setting up the toolbar drive buttons with text and images, using the system small image list, which the toolbar won't destroy on its own.

I'm settling the layout details: the toolbar's own height sets the drive bar, and the rest of the panel stacks around it at DPI-scaled sizes. The system small image list is fine to share since neither the toolbar nor the listview will destroy it. For the header and status labels, I just need to handle the static control colors and keep the status text plain.

I'm sizing the layout rows now: the drive bar takes the toolbar's button height plus a little padding, and the tab row follows the first tab item's bottom edge. The header and status labels each get the text height plus a small margin, and the command-line row will use the combo box's height once it's created.

I'm setting the font height aside and turning to the main toolbar: it'll load the standard, view, and history bitmaps, and I'm sketching out the button list, including back, forward, and favorites.

Continuing the toolbar setup, I'm listing the standard, view, and history image indices I want for the main buttons, covering the usual clipboard, undo, delete, file, print, find and sort icons along with the parent-folder, network and new-folder ones.

Now I'm laying out the main toolbar buttons: back, forward, and up on the first group, then copy, cut, and paste, followed by new folder, delete, and properties. Sort buttons for name, type, size, and date come next, then a new-tab button and a console button using the file-open icon.

I'm skipping a dedicated console button in the toolbar, since that action already lives in the Commands menu as "Open console" and opens cmd.exe in the current directory. For tooltips, I'll let the toolbar send TTN_GETDISPINFO to the main window keyed by command id and return the text there. I'm keeping the 16px icons even at high DPI, since they're small but workable, and then I'll check the toolchain.

data.text:
The user is asking me to build POSCommander2, a Total Commander-like Win32 file manager, from scratch using mingw-w64 GCC 16.1.0 with CMake, Ninja, gdb and windres, since no MSVC is available. I confirm the MinGW headers ship full Win32 and COM headers including shobjidl.h and IFileOperation, so a native, small, fast app builds fine. I check the header greps returned nothing visible, likely output formatting, and check the paths properly.

I set the build up: C++17/20, Win32 API, CMake + Ninja, mingw-w64 GCC working in VS Code with CMake tools. I make it Unicode, DPI-aware, with a comctl32 v6 manifest. Two panels use ListView in LVS_REPORT virtual (owner-data, LVS_OWNERDATA) mode with LVS_EX_FULLROWSELECT and LVS_EX_DOUBLEBUFFER, plus GDI-drawn arrows in the toolbar, tabs, drive bar, command line, F-key bar, status bar, menu and toolbar. Total Commander appearance is mostly native: white list, gray header, blue selection.

Core work: directory enumeration with FindFirstFileEx, natural sort, tabs, navigation, F3 viewer, F5 copy via IFileOperation for the native progress with pause, F6 move, F7 mkdir, F8 delete to the recycle bin via IFileOperation with FOF_ALLOWUNDO, Shift+F6 rename, Alt+F7 search, the IContextMenu context menu, and shell icons through SHGetFileInfo with the system image list. This is a big job, so I deliver a substantial but coherent implementation that compiles and runs, checking correctness by compiling locally with g++ and launching the exe on the user's desktop session for a smoke check and screenshot capture.

The codebase: CMakeLists.txt plus src/main.cpp (WinMain, window, menu, layout, message loop), src/panel.cpp/.h (listview, tabs, drive bar, path, enumeration, sorting), src/fs.h/.cpp (enumeration, natural compare, formatting, drives), src/shellops.cpp/.h (image list, context menu, IFileOperation ops), src/viewer.cpp, and src/res/app.rc with app.manifest and a generated app.ico. Link libraries: comctl32, shlwapi, shell32, ole32, uuid, comdlg32, user32, gdi32, advapi32. I define wWinMain and pass -municode plus -static -static-libgcc -static-libstdc++ so the exe is small and portable.

In the virtual listview the control manages selection; I query it with LVM_GETITEMSTATE and preserve cursor and selection across refreshes by saving names before LVM_SETITEMCOUNT. Columns are Имя, Тип, Размер, Дата; I set the system small image list with LVM_SETIMAGELIST. The "Тип" column shows the uppercase extension, "Папка" or "Файл". Header clicks toggle the sort column and direction.

Panel internals: a single "POPanelHead" child window of height 44 draws the drive bar and tab strip and handles clicks; the listview fills the rest. Below the two panels sits the command line (24px), the F-key bar (22px) and the status bar (22px). Menus are created in code with CreateMenu and AppendMenuW with Russian labels, so the .rc file holds only the icon and manifest and avoids encoding problems. A small modal input dialog, PromptText, handles F7, rename and copy/move targets. Settings persist to an ini in %APPDATA%.

data.text:
I'm laying out the project's architecture before writing anything: a CMake build with presets, VS Code task and launch configs, Windows resources including a generated icon, and a `main.cpp` containing WinMain and the message loop.

I'm working through the remaining source files: the main window layout, the panel with its virtual list view, the filesystem enumeration, and the shell integration for icons, context menus and file operations.

I'm planning the viewer's controls: switching between hex and text, choosing encodings like ANSI, OEM and UTF-8 with key shortcuts, closing on Escape, and capping how much of a large file goes into the edit control. Then I'm working out the dialogs, where rename will use in-place label editing on the owner-data list view and the copy and mkdir inputs will come from .rc dialog templates.

I'm checking how windres handles UTF-8 in the resource file, since `#pragma code_page(65001)` should work with a recent binutils. If that turns out broken, I'd fall back to setting the Russian strings in code at WM_INITDIALOG. I'm also planning a Search dialog for Alt+F7 with mask, text and start directory fields.

I'm sketching the toolbar next, using the standard system bitmaps for Refresh, Back, Forward, Up, Copy, Move, New folder, Delete, Find and Properties. Then I'm turning to the per-panel drive buttons, which will sit above each panel the way Total Commander does it.

I'm moving on to the panel's details: a drive combo with the free-space line, then tabs, a path header with history and hotlist buttons, the file list with its name, type, size and date columns, and a status line showing sizes and counts. I'm weighing whether to add the optional vertical button bar between the panels, leaning toward skipping it at first and keeping the layout simple.

I'm setting up the per-panel drive bar as a toolbar with list-style buttons using the system small image list, then a drive combo with a free-space line beside it, plus "\" and ".." buttons. Next I'm turning to tabs: a tab control above the path header, one tab per directory, with Ctrl+T, Ctrl+W and Ctrl+Tab for new, close and next.

I'm planning the list view as a virtual report-mode control with owner data, so the cursor is the single highlighted row and marked files get tracked separately and drawn in red through custom draw. For drive labels I'm going with a "letter:folder" style like "e:net10.0", and just "e:" for the root.

I'm working out the keyboard and mouse model for the panel: Insert or Space to mark a file, Num+ and Num- for mask selection, Ctrl+A to select all, and Shift+Up/Down to mark a range while moving. For the mouse, a plain click moves the cursor, Ctrl+click toggles a mark, Shift+click marks a range, and right-click opens the context menu.

Next I'm considering how the cursor and marks should look in a list that uses a single selection, with custom drawing needed for the rest.

I'm working out how custom draw will color marked rows red while the cursor row is still highlighted. The idea is to clear the selected state during item prepaint and paint the background myself, though I'm still unsure whether a full-row background applies across every subitem in report mode.

I'm figuring out how the custom draw should handle the cursor row: a light blue background when the panel is active, with the text turned red if the row is marked. The plan is to skip the Explorer theme so the classic list view keeps the full-row background, and I'm still checking whether the focus rectangle should stay visible.

I'm working out how to get the cursor row's highlight suppressed in custom draw, so the marked-red text can show without the system selection color overriding it. The plan is to track the cursor index myself through the focused item, compare it during prepaint, and strip the selected flag from the item state before setting the background. I'm also keeping LVS_SINGLESEL on so the list only ever has one highlighted row.

I'm settling the icons next: the shared system image list gets pulled from SHGetFileInfo with the system-index flags and assigned to the list view as its small-icon list, and I need LVS_SHAREIMAGELISTS so the control doesn't destroy it on close. Item text comes from the owner-data callback, with folders showing an "<Папка>" size and the ".." row taking the current directory's date.

I'm deciding how to get icons for each file without slowing the listing down: generic extensions can use cached system icons by type, while executables, shortcuts and icon files need their own icon read. For those special cases I'm weighing a lazy lookup for just the visible rows against a background thread that posts the icon back once it's ready, since network drives would make the synchronous version sluggish.

I'm settling the icon approach: each entry will hold a cache slot starting at -1, filled lazily only for visible rows, and I'm keeping it simple rather than adding a background worker. Hidden files will get the ghosted cut state through the owner-data item state.

I'm settling the sorting: names will use natural ordering with folders first and ".." at the top, plus sorting by extension, size, and date, toggled by header clicks and Ctrl+F3 to F6. I'm also planning to start reading the directory with FindFirst.

I'm deciding to keep the directory read synchronous for now, since local listings of around ten thousand files should only take milliseconds, and I'll note the possible network stall in the README. Then I'm turning to automatic refresh: each panel gets a watcher thread that wakes on change notifications so the listing updates when the folder changes.

I'm planning to refresh the panels when the directory changes, using a watcher that debounces the notifications. For copying, I'm opening a dialog that asks for the target path, defaulting to the other panel, and then handing the work to the native shell copy with its progress and conflict handling. A single file copied to a non-existent target will be treated as a rename.

I'm now planning the file operations: F6 for moving, with Shift+F6 doing an in-place rename through the list view's label editor, keeping the extension out of the selection. F7 will create directories, including nested paths, and move the cursor to the new one. For deletion, I'm looking at a confirmation prompt followed by a recycle-bin delete through the shell.

I'm mapping out the rest of the file operations: F3 and F4 open the file in a viewer or editor, with notepad as the default that the ini can override. Enter opens folders in the panel and runs files through the shell. Backspace and Ctrl+PgUp go up a level, Ctrl+\ jumps to the root, and Alt+Left/Right step through history. I'm also adding Alt+F1/Alt+F2 for a drive menu on each panel, plus Ctrl+R to refresh and a Ctrl+Right shortcut that opens the directory in the other panel.

I'm now settling the keyboard side: Ctrl+Left/Right will point the other panel at the cursor folder, Ctrl+U swaps the panels, and Ctrl+D will pop up a hotlist from the ini with an option to add the current directory. Typing letters will go to the command line, and Ctrl+Enter will paste the filename there, with Enter running command-line input through the shell in the current directory.

I'm settling the rest of the keyboard behavior: Enter will try to run the typed command through the shell in the current directory, falling back to a cmd prompt if that fails. Ctrl+letter quick search is the last thing on the list.

I'm weighing how to handle quick search: TC defaults to Ctrl+Alt+letters, while plain letters are already routed to the command line. I'm considering a small status-text buffer that resets after a second, versus a popup edit box under the panel.

I'm wrapping up the selection shortcuts: Num+ and Num- for masks, Num* to invert, and Ctrl+A or Ctrl+Num+ and Ctrl+Num- for select-all and clear. Space will mark a folder and compute its size on a worker thread that posts the result back, and Alt+Shift+Enter will do that for every folder in the listing.

I'm settling the display formats now: sizes under 1024 bytes show as bytes, larger ones as Кб, Мб or Гб with one decimal and a comma, and dates use dd.MM.yy HH:mm. After that I'll look at the drive info.

I'm settling on drive info: the status line will show the volume label and free space for the current drive, but I'll only query that when navigating, since removable and network drives can be slow. Drive lists and types are cheap, so those I'll fetch freely, and drive icons will come from stock system icons rather than touching the drives themselves.

I'm laying out the main window from the top down: a menu bar with the usual Total Commander groups plus a Вкладки menu, then the toolbar, then a drive bar above each panel.

I'm finishing the layout plan: a splitter between the panels that drags to resize and doubles back to an even split, followed by the fonts, which I'm taking from the system message font.

I'm going with the system message font throughout and handling DPI by reading the scale at startup, then updating the font and layout when it changes. I'm leaving the list background at the standard system white rather than the grey from the screenshot, since that looks like a user color setting. The path header will be a highlighted bar in the active caption color.

I'm settling on the path header's look: a bar in the active panel that's light blue with dark text, and a greyer one for the inactive panel, drawn as a custom-painted child window.

I'm settling the path header's details: clicking a segment of the path will jump to that folder, and the "*" and "▼" buttons on the right will open the hotlist and history.

I'm settling the input routing now: keys get intercepted in the message loop before dispatch, and when a printable character reaches a panel's list view without Ctrl or Alt, I'll move focus to the command line and forward the character there, while keeping that panel marked as active.

I'm settling the input routing: while the command line has focus, the arrow keys, PgUp/PgDn and Insert still go to the active panel's list, and the function keys work globally except inside modal dialogs, which run their own loop.

I'm settling the keyboard handling for the list views: they already handle arrows, Home/End and paging, but I'll intercept Shift+Up/Down to mark items. Esc will clear the command line, and Ctrl+Down will open its history dropdown, which is a combobox that keeps past commands.

I'm handling the mouse side of the list views next: double-click opens an item, right-click brings up the shell context menu, and clicking a column header sorts. Ctrl-click toggles a mark and Shift-click selects a range. Drag-and-drop is left out of this first version.

I'm working out the context menu next: for the marked items in one folder, I'll bind the shell folder, get each child's IContextMenu, and show it with TrackPopupMenu. Submenus like Send To and Open With will need the menu-message forwarding handled as well.

I'm covering the remaining context-menu details: forwarding menu messages to the active IContextMenu2/3 so submenus like Send To work, and skipping the background menu for empty space. Shift+F10 and the Apps key will open the menu at the cursor item. For properties, I'll invoke the "properties" verb on the marked items' context menu so it works for multiple selections too, and then I'm moving on to clipboard shortcuts.

content.text:
I'm laying out the project's architecture before writing anything: a CMake build with presets, VS Code task and launch configs, Windows resources including a generated icon, and a `main.cpp` containing WinMain and the message loop.

I'm working through the remaining source files: the main window layout, the panel with its virtual list view, the filesystem enumeration, and the shell integration for icons, context menus and file operations.

I'm planning the viewer's controls: switching between hex and text, choosing encodings like ANSI, OEM and UTF-8 with key shortcuts, closing on Escape, and capping how much of a large file goes into the edit control. Then I'm working out the dialogs, where rename will use in-place label editing on the owner-data list view and the copy and mkdir inputs will come from .rc dialog templates.

I'm checking how windres handles UTF-8 in the resource file, since `#pragma code_page(65001)` should work with a recent binutils. If that turns out broken, I'd fall back to setting the Russian strings in code at WM_INITDIALOG. I'm also planning a Search dialog for Alt+F7 with mask, text and start directory fields.

I'm sketching the toolbar next, using the standard system bitmaps for Refresh, Back, Forward, Up, Copy, Move, New folder, Delete, Find and Properties. Then I'm turning to the per-panel drive buttons, which will sit above each panel the way Total Commander does it.

I'm moving on to the panel's details: a drive combo with the free-space line, then tabs, a path header with history and hotlist buttons, the file list with its name, type, size and date columns, and a status line showing sizes and counts. I'm weighing whether to add the optional vertical button bar between the panels, leaning toward skipping it at first and keeping the layout simple.

I'm setting up the per-panel drive bar as a toolbar with list-style buttons using the system small image list, then a drive combo with a free-space line beside it, plus "\" and ".." buttons. Next I'm turning to tabs: a tab control above the path header, one tab per directory, with Ctrl+T, Ctrl+W and Ctrl+Tab for new, close and next.

I'm planning the list view as a virtual report-mode control with owner data, so the cursor is the single highlighted row and marked files get tracked separately and drawn in red through custom draw. For drive labels I'm going with a "letter:folder" style like "e:net10.0", and just "e:" for the root.

I'm working out the keyboard and mouse model for the panel: Insert or Space to mark a file, Num+ and Num- for mask selection, Ctrl+A to select all, and Shift+Up/Down to mark a range while moving. For the mouse, a plain click moves the cursor, Ctrl+click toggles a mark, Shift+click marks a range, and right-click opens the context menu.

Next I'm considering how the cursor and marks should look in a list that uses a single selection, with custom drawing needed for the rest.

I'm working out how custom draw will color marked rows red while the cursor row is still highlighted. The idea is to clear the selected state during item prepaint and paint the background myself, though I'm still unsure whether a full-row background applies across every subitem in report mode.

I'm figuring out how the custom draw should handle the cursor row: a light blue background when the panel is active, with the text turned red if the row is marked. The plan is to skip the Explorer theme so the classic list view keeps the full-row background, and I'm still checking whether the focus rectangle should stay visible.

I'm working out how to get the cursor row's highlight suppressed in custom draw, so the marked-red text can show without the system selection color overriding it. The plan is to track the cursor index myself through the focused item, compare it during prepaint, and strip the selected flag from the item state before setting the background. I'm also keeping LVS_SINGLESEL on so the list only ever has one highlighted row.

I'm settling the icons next: the shared system image list gets pulled from SHGetFileInfo with the system-index flags and assigned to the list view as its small-icon list, and I need LVS_SHAREIMAGELISTS so the control doesn't destroy it on close. Item text comes from the owner-data callback, with folders showing an "<Папка>" size and the ".." row taking the current directory's date.

I'm deciding how to get icons for each file without slowing the listing down: generic extensions can use cached system icons by type, while executables, shortcuts and icon files need their own icon read. For those special cases I'm weighing a lazy lookup for just the visible rows against a background thread that posts the icon back once it's ready, since network drives would make the synchronous version sluggish.

I'm settling the icon approach: each entry will hold a cache slot starting at -1, filled lazily only for visible rows, and I'm keeping it simple rather than adding a background worker. Hidden files will get the ghosted cut state through the owner-data item state.

I'm settling the sorting: names will use natural ordering with folders first and ".." at the top, plus sorting by extension, size, and date, toggled by header clicks and Ctrl+F3 to F6. I'm also planning to start reading the directory with FindFirst.

I'm deciding to keep the directory read synchronous for now, since local listings of around ten thousand files should only take milliseconds, and I'll note the possible network stall in the README. Then I'm turning to automatic refresh: each panel gets a watcher thread that wakes on change notifications so the listing updates when the folder changes.

I'm planning to refresh the panels when the directory changes, using a watcher that debounces the notifications. Still writing the viewer's codepage and hex switches: I'm making the codepage change keep the current position by remembering the top line's byte offset, rebuilding the line index in text mode, and resetting any search highlight.
