I'm going to write the actual project now, since this is a large task. My plan is a CMake-based layout with presets for Ninja and GCC, VS Code settings, and some documentation files, which I'll build with MinGW.

Still listing the source files for the project: the app entry point, main window, file panel, file system enumeration, formatting, shell integration, a read-only viewer, and input dialogs.

Next I'm planning the dialogs as .rc resources, with a search dialog for Alt+F7 that runs in a worker thread and lists results. Config will go into a portable INI file next to the exe, saving window position, tabs, paths, column widths, and sort order.

I'm working out the toolbar next: standard system bitmaps for the common actions, with buttons for refresh, back and forward, copy, move, new folder, delete, search, properties, a command prompt, and Notepad. Each panel will also get a row of drive buttons plus a line showing the working folder's free space.

I'm laying out the rest of the panel: a row of function-key buttons along the bottom (F3 view through F8 delete, plus Alt+F4 to exit), with a command line above them. Each panel is a virtual-mode ListView in report style with its own column headers and a status line at the bottom.

I'm settling on the ListView approach: report style with virtual data, so the native header handles sort arrows and column resizing. Since the ListView's own selection can't carry TC's cursor-versus-mark distinction, I'll keep marks in a separate set and color them through custom draw, with the cursor as the single-select highlight.

I'm working out the keyboard and mouse behavior next: Insert toggles the mark on the cursor item and moves down, Space toggles it too, and Num+, Num- and Num* handle selection by mask or inversion. For the mouse, plain clicks move the cursor, Ctrl+click toggles marks, and Shift+click marks a range, which means subclassing the ListView to intercept those clicks before the default selection behavior takes over.

I'm settling the keyboard and mouse handling: the list gets subclassed so Ctrl-click toggles a mark and Shift-click marks a range before default selection kicks in, and keys like Enter, Backspace, Tab, Insert, Space, the function keys and Delete get intercepted first. I'm keeping the native ListView for its header, scrolling and keyboard navigation rather than custom-drawing the whole panel.

Now I'm settling on how keys get routed: rather than handling them one list at a time, I'm planning to check each message in the main loop before translation, sending panel and command-line keys through a single central handler. That approach fits the classic commander layout, where typed letters go to the command line.

I'm wiring the message loop so each key press gets checked before translation, passing it to the app's handler when focus is in the main window and not a dialog. Typed letters in the file list go to the command line instead of moving the cursor, Enter runs the command if there is one and otherwise opens the item, Backspace trims the command line before it goes up a folder, and Esc clears it.

I'm working out how the command line gets run: a "cd" command will just change the panel's folder, and anything else will go to CreateProcess in the panel's current directory, with ShellExecute as the fallback for documents and links.

I'm settling on how the command line runs things: Enter tries ShellExecute on the first token with the rest as parameters, falling back to a cmd window if that fails, and Shift+Enter goes straight to cmd so the window stays open. The command history will live in a dropdown combo and be saved to the INI file. For the path header, I'm leaning toward a simple static control with ellipsis truncation rather than a custom-painted child.

I'm settling the path header now: the active panel's header gets a blue background with white text, and a click just activates the panel. A double-click will open an in-place edit over the header that navigates on Enter and tears down on Escape or focus loss. Next to it go a hotlist button bound to Ctrl+D and a history dropdown. I'm also starting on the per-panel drive bar, with a button for each drive plus root and parent.

I'm wiring up the per-panel drive bar as a toolbar with the system drive icons, marking the current drive with a check-group button. A static control beside it will show the free space, and I need to rebuild the bar whenever a drive is added or removed.

Now I'm working out the tab strip: labels that show the drive letter and folder name, like "e:gui_project", with double-click or middle-click closing a tab. Ctrl+T opens a new one, Ctrl+W closes it, and Ctrl+Tab switches between them. I'm leaning toward always showing the strip rather than hiding it when there's only one tab, since that keeps the layout simpler.

Now I'm settling the panel's columns: name, type, size and date, with the name shown without its extension and the extension in its own column. Directory rows will show "<Папка>" for size, and the first row will be "..". The date will follow a dd.mm.yy hh:mm pattern, and sizes will switch units dynamically rather than staying fixed to bytes.

Next I'm settling the sort order: directories always come first, sorted by name, and files follow using whichever column was clicked. Name sorting uses natural order, extension sorting falls back to name, and dates and sizes compare directly. Reversing the direction just flips the comparison, and ".." stays pinned at the top. For the icons, I'll pull the shared system image list through SHGetFileInfo so each row shows the right shell icon.

Now I'm planning the icon handling: regular files will take their icon from the system image list by extension and cache it, while executables, shortcuts and similar types get looked up individually in a background thread, and folders just use the generic folder icon.

I'm setting up the icon loader as a single background worker thread that takes requests with a target window, generation, item index and path, so per-file icons for executables don't stall scrolling. Each result gets posted back to the panel with the generation and the item and icon indices packed together.

I'm weighing how to get icon results back to the panel: a heap-allocated result struct posted to the window, or a mutex-guarded queue. The pointer approach is simpler. Since sorting reorders items, I'm now thinking the icon request should refer to a stable entry id rather than the displayed index.

I'm settling the panel's data model: a master list of entries in load order, plus a sorted view of indices into it, with marks and icons stored on each entry. Icon requests will reference the entry's position in the master list, and each reload bumps a generation counter so stale icon results get ignored. I'm also weighing whether a synchronous directory read is fast enough locally, which it likely is, though network folders could stall.

Now I'm setting up the auto-refresh: a change-notification handle on the panel's folder, waited on alongside the other handles in the message loop. When it signals, a short debounce timer will fire and reload the panel while keeping the cursor and marks in place.

Still working out the message loop: waiting on the directory change handles alongside the window messages, and calling back into the app when one fires. Once handled, the notification gets re-armed and the loop carries on. I'm also thinking about the debounce, so a burst of file changes during a copy triggers a single reload.

I'm working out how the file operations will run: copy and move through F5 and F6 with an editable target path, handled by IFileOperation so the native progress and conflict dialogs come for free. The open question is whether calling it straight from the UI thread is safe, since it may pump messages internally.

I'm weighing whether to run the file operation on a background thread so the UI doesn't freeze during the copy, since PerformOperations blocks the caller. Leaning toward a worker thread with the main window as owner, though cross-thread ownership brings its own input-queue concerns I still need to check.

Now I'm settling on the worker-thread route for the copy, and I'll pass the main window as owner so the progress and conflict dialogs stay attached to it. Once the operation finishes, I'll post a completion message so the panels refresh, though the change notifications would catch that anyway. For a copy into a target from the dialog, if the target is an existing folder, I'll call CopyItem with that folder as the destination.

I'm working out the copy target logic: if the destination ends in a backslash or is an existing folder, the files go into it, and for a single file the typed name can rename it on the way. For a missing parent or multiple sources I'll create the folder first. Next I'm settling delete on F8 and Del, with a confirmation prompt and the recycle bin via IFileOperation.

I'm settling the delete behavior now: plain F8/Del sends items to the recycle bin silently through IFileOperation, and Shift+Del skips the bin and the undo option. Renaming on Shift+F6 will use in-place label editing, though I still need to work out how the extension-less display of the name column fits with that.

I'm settling how the rename works: Shift+F6 turns the name into an in-place edit box with the extension left out of the selection, and on finish it moves the file and puts the cursor on the new name. The one thing left to handle is that a plain click on an already-selected item shouldn't start an edit, so I'll cancel that case in the begin-edit handler.

I'm adding a new-folder command on F7 that asks for a name through an input dialog and creates the folder, including any missing parents, then moves the cursor onto it. For F3 I'm building a read-only viewer window around a multiline edit control, loading the file in Consolas and capping how much gets read so large files don't exhaust memory.

I'm settling the viewer's text handling: it detects UTF-8 or UTF-16 from the byte order mark and otherwise falls back to the ANSI code page. I'm also deciding which keys close the window and planning a W toggle for word wrap, though I'm leaving the encoding switch keys and find function for later.

I'm settling the viewer's controls now: A switches to ANSI (CP1251), S to DOS (CP866), and U to UTF-8, with W toggling word wrap and Esc closing the window. For binary content I'll swap NUL bytes for a visible dot so the edit control doesn't stop early, and I'm leaving image preview out of this first version.

I'm handling the viewer's keys through a general pre-translate hook: the message loop finds the root window of whatever has focus and, if that window is a viewer, lets it take the key before the edit control swallows it. The search dialog will stay modal, with its results posted back to the dialog window.

Now I'm planning the F4 edit command: it'll open the file in an editor set in the config, falling back to notepad, via ShellExecute. For Alt+F7 search I'm building a modal dialog with a start point, a file mask (defaulting to *.* and accepting ';' or spaces as separators), and an optional text field, with a results list where double-clicking jumps the panel to the file. A worker thread will walk the folders with FindFirstFileEx and match masks using PathMatchSpec.

I'm working out the text search: it'll look for the needle encoded as UTF-8, CP1251 and UTF-16LE, reading files in chunks. I'm still deciding whether matching should be case-insensitive for ASCII and Cyrillic.

I'm settling the search's case handling: for Cyrillic in the ANSI encoding I'll lowercase both the needle and the buffer through a lookup table, while for UTF-8 I'm only planning ASCII case folding, since full Cyrillic folding there is harder.

I'm settling the UTF-8 case folding for the search: for Cyrillic I'll remap the two-byte sequences in place, moving capital letters to their lowercase forms and leaving the byte count unchanged. Because the length stays the same, I can overlap chunks by needle length minus one and still catch matches that straddle a boundary.

I'm wrapping up the text search design: UTF-16 matching is being skipped for now, and the file reading will use 1 MB blocks with the tail of each block carried into the next. Results will go into a mutex-protected list that the dialog drains with a 100 ms timer, which avoids flooding the message queue. I still need to work out how the right-click context menu gets its shell menu.

I'm now settling the context menu: I'll get the shell's menu for the selected items by binding the folder as an IShellFolder and resolving the child PIDLs. The menu gets built with QueryContextMenu, shown with TrackPopupMenu, and the chosen command is run through InvokeCommand.

I'm wiring up the context menu's remaining pieces: for the background menu on empty space, I'd get the current folder's IShellFolder and ask it for its own IContextMenu, reusing the same tracking code. After that I'm moving on to the Alt+Enter properties command via SHObjectProperties.

Now I'm working out how drag and drop fits in: the file list would start an OLE drag from its selected items, probably through the shell's data object, though I'm leaving that for after the first version.

Now I'm planning drag and drop: the file list will start an OLE drag from the selected items through the shell data object, with a drop target that forwards to the folder's own drop handler. I'll call OleInitialize on the UI thread so RegisterDragDrop works, though the scope is getting large and I'll need to be careful about correctness.

I'm checking which compiler quirks to expect with MinGW, since mingw-w64 does provide IFileOperation and I may need a fallback define for FOFX_RECYCLEONDELETE. I'll confirm the shell and COM headers compile before going further.

I'm settling the project's remaining details now: the window DPI handling, using per-monitor awareness through the manifest, and scaling sizes with the window's current DPI. For fonts, I'll take the system message font, and when the DPI changes I'll rebuild the fonts, relayout, and apply the suggested window rect.

I'm settling the ListView's look now: I'll skip the Explorer theme so the cursor row keeps the classic solid highlight, and paint the focused row in a light blue through custom draw for the active panel.

Now I'm working on the custom draw for the list view: I'll clear the selected and focus states so my own colors show, and paint the cursor row differently when it belongs to the active panel. Marked entries get their own text color.

Next I'm making the ListView draw the cursor row myself: clearing the selected and focus states so my own colors show, painting the cursor in a different shade for the active panel, and keeping selection tied to the cursor row.

I'm checking whether clearing the selected state in custom draw still works once the themed ListView is in use, since I remember comctl v6 may ignore that change. A safer route might be to turn off the visual theme on the list so the classic highlight behaves predictably.

Now I'm weighing whether to disable the list's visual theme or draw every row myself. Owner-drawing the whole row, with icons and each column's text placed by the header widths, gives the most control and should be fast enough.

Now I'm planning to custom-draw each row myself: a background fill, the shell icon placed at the left edge, and each column's text right-aligned or left-aligned within the header widths, with ellipsis for overflow. I'll paint the cursor row's background in its own color and leave the list font as the list already set it.

I'm going to draw the inactive panel's cursor as a dotted focus-style frame, while the active panel gets a filled light blue bar. The "..", the parent-directory row, needs an icon too, and I'm weighing a folder icon against drawing a simple arrow myself, since loading a shell32 icon by index feels unreliable.

Now I'm handling the mouse in the list subclass, starting with the left button: if Ctrl is held, I toggle the mark on the item under the cursor, move the cursor there, and skip the default handling so no drag begins.

Now I'm handling the mouse and keyboard in the list: a Shift-click marks the range from the cursor to the clicked row, a right-click opens the context menu through WM_CONTEXTMENU, and receiving focus makes that panel the active one.

I'm mapping out the keyboard handling for the panels: Tab switches panels, Enter runs the command line if it has text or otherwise opens the cursor item, and Backspace either edits the command line or goes up a folder. Insert and Space would toggle the mark on the cursor item, and I'm still deciding whether Space should also compute a folder's size.

I'm weighing whether to compute directory sizes in a background thread and post the result back to the panel, with Space marking the item when the command line is empty. For the selection keys I'm planning the numpad shortcuts: Num+ and Num- for group select and unselect, Num* to invert, and Ctrl+A to select all.

Now I'm working through the remaining keyboard shortcuts: F2 or Ctrl+R to refresh, F3 through F8 for the usual file operations, and Delete when the command line is empty. Shift+F5 would copy within the same panel with the name prefilled, Alt+F1 and Alt+F2 open a drive menu for each panel, and Alt+F7 starts a search.

I'm mapping the remaining shortcuts: Alt+Left and Alt+Right for history, Alt+Down for the history dropdown, and Ctrl+D for the hotlist. Tabs get Ctrl+T to open and Ctrl+W to close, with Ctrl+Tab cycling between them, while Ctrl+U swaps the panels. For sorting, Ctrl+F3 through Ctrl+F6 map to name, extension, date, and size, and Ctrl+H toggles hidden files.

I'm going to handle the remaining keys in the list: Esc clears the command line, and typing letters feeds the command line. I'm weighing a quick-search feature on Alt+letters, though that may clash with menu mnemonics, so I'm leaning toward a Ctrl+Alt variant instead.

I'm now planning the quick search feature: Ctrl+Alt plus a letter opens a small floating edit at the bottom of the panel that moves the cursor to the first prefix match, closing on Esc or Enter. I'm leaning toward keeping that version basic, since the project is already large, and then I'll move on to laying out the menu command IDs.

I'm settling on building the menus and dialogs in code rather than through a resource file, since that avoids codepage problems with the Russian text. Dialogs will be assembled as an in-memory template through a small helper class.

I'm settling on a small in-memory dialog template builder for the dialogs, so they get native Tab and Enter/Esc handling. The resource file will only carry the icon, manifest, and version info, with ASCII strings there.

Writing CMake config with compile definitions and warning flags...

Writing CMake link settings and compile flags for the MinGW build...

Now I'm settling on Win32 threads with CreateThread and an SRWLOCK wrapper instead of std::thread or std::mutex, since the MinGW thread model may not support them reliably. Executable size should stay small with static linking and -Os.

Now I'm settling the config file: it goes next to the executable if that folder is writable, otherwise under the user's AppData. The saved state covers window placement, both panels' tabs and active tab, sort settings, column widths, the hidden-files toggle, command history, the hotlist, and the editor path. Then I'll turn to the per-panel drive toolbar, which needs the shared system image list set up.

Now I'm setting up the toolbar for the drive buttons: each one shows a short text label beside its icon, using the shared system image list, and I'm working out the list-style and mixed-button flags needed to make the labels appear.

I'm setting the drive toolbar's buttons to use the drive letter as their label, with a root button and an up button alongside. Each panel is its own container window that holds the toolbar, tab control, path header, listview, and status line, so the listview's notifications route through the panel.

Now I'm laying out the rest of the main window: a thin draggable splitter between the two panels, a command line with the current path and an input combobox, and a row of F-key buttons along the bottom. The buttons will be plain push buttons, and after a command runs I'll return focus to the active panel's list. I'm also starting on the main toolbar, planning to load the standard small color icons for it.

Now I'm choosing the main toolbar icons: I'll load the standard small color bitmaps from comctl32 and pick out the copy, delete, find, and properties images, plus the parent folder, new folder, details, and sort-by-name images for the view buttons, and the back and forward history images.

I'm checking how the toolbar image list offsets work when I load the standard bitmaps, since the return value of TB_LOADIMAGES is unclear to me, so I'll switch to TB_ADDBITMAP and take the starting index from there.

Now I'm settling on the toolbar bitmaps: TB_ADDBITMAP will take the standard, view, and history image sets, using their counts as the button ranges. The old comctl32 bitmaps may look dated at high DPI, but they'll do. For the main toolbar's refresh and other buttons I'm checking which of those sets has a matching image.

Now I'm laying out the main toolbar buttons, Back and Forward first, and I'm choosing which of the standard history, view, and file images to use for the rest.

Now I'm picking the remaining main toolbar buttons: a favorites button, plus an extra one for opening a console or editor, and I'm still deciding which standard icon fits best for it.

Next I'm settling the menu contents: File gets Open, View, Edit, Copy, Move, New folder, Delete, permanent delete, rename, and properties, each with its shortcut. The network-drive connect button and a refresh button using the redo icon will go on the main toolbar too.

Now I'm laying out the Help and Navigation menus, which group the selection commands, copy-name actions, and things like file search, favorite directories, history, and parent or root navigation with their shortcuts.

Now I'm listing the menu entries for the Navigation group: swapping panels, the same-folder option without a hotkey, and the network drive connect and disconnect commands.

Now I'm working out the menu contents: the Navigation group covers tabs, the favorites list, history, and parent or root navigation, and I'm still deciding on the rest of the menus.

Now I'm working out how keys get routed: when focus sits in a panel list or the command line, panel-specific keys apply, while F-keys and similar work across the main window. I need to leave in-place rename edits alone, since their Enter and Escape belong to the edit control.

Now I'm working out the key routing for the command line edit: Enter runs the command, Esc clears it and returns focus to the list, Tab moves focus back to the panel, and the F-keys get handled since they carry no text meaning. Other focus targets, like the in-place rename edit or quick search, I'll leave alone.

Now I'm sketching the Panel class interface: creation tied to a parent window and app, navigation with an optional focus target and history flag, reload that keeps state, and accessors for the path, the selected names and paths, and the cursor entry. I'm also including the mark-and-select helpers.

Now I'm sketching the tab and history bookkeeping for each panel: each tab keeps its own path, back and forward stacks, sort settings, and the name to focus, and Alt+Down will show a popup of recent paths built from the back stack.

Next I'm settling path handling: drive roots like "C:\" stay as they are, and Up does nothing from a root or a UNC share. I'm normalizing paths with GetFullPathNameW, dropping trailing backslashes except on roots, and adding a helper that prefixes long paths for enumeration and file operations, while leaving shell-based operations to handle their own paths.

Now I'm defining the file entry struct: a name, size, modification time, attributes, a cached icon index, the extension offset, and flags for directory, the parent entry, and marking. For directories I'm leaving out the extension, while for files the extension starts at the last dot, except for names that begin with a dot.

Now I'm covering the file size and free-space display: a drive's volume label and its free and total space go in one line, and I'm caching the volume info per root so network drives don't stall every navigation. I'm also noting that the drive list will come from the logical drives bitmask, with each drive's icon taken from the shell.

Now I'm deciding how to get the drive icons: local and removable drives can use a real shell lookup, but for remote drives that might stall on a disconnected share, so I'm considering a stock icon instead.

Now I'm settling on the drive and folder icons: instead of asking the shell for each drive, which could stall on a disconnected network share, I'll use stock system icons chosen by drive type, plus a stock folder icon.

Now I'm settling how file icons get looked up: I'll use the shell's extension-based lookup, which is fast, and keep the results in a cache on the UI thread. Files like executables, shortcuts, and icon files can't share one icon per extension, so those will show a generic icon at first and be resolved later.

Now I'm deciding how the background icon loader handles requests: it'll take them from a queue shared with the UI thread, and the newest requests, which are the visible rows, get served first.

Now I'm working out the background icon loader's result path: each finished lookup gets posted back to the window with its entry index and icon index packed into one 64-bit parameter, and I'm adding a compile-time check that the build is 64-bit. I'm also dropping the idea of custom folder icons for now. Directory size calculation is next, starting from its own thread and reporting results back the same way.

Writing context menu code...

Now I'm getting the shell's context menu for the selected files: I'll bind the folder through the desktop folder rather than SHBindToObject, then parse each name into a child item ID and request the menu from the folder, or a background menu if nothing is selected.

Still writing the context menu code: the next part gets the menu from the shell, tracks it at the cursor, and reads the chosen verb, returning early if it's "rename".

Still writing the context menu code: I'm invoking the chosen command with the folder as the working directory and the modifier keys passed along, then freeing the item IDs.

Now I'm wrapping up the context menu helper: I need to release the item IDs and the shell folder reference, and I'm also adding a background-menu option so New and Paste are available from empty space. For clipboard copy and cut, I'll reuse the same menu plumbing through an InvokeVerb helper that calls QueryContextMenu before InvokeCommand.

Now I'm looking at drag and drop: when a drag starts, I'll gather the selected names, or just the dragged item if it isn't marked, and ask the shell folder for a data object to hand to the drag-drop call.

Now I'm looking at drag and drop on the target side: I'll register a drop target on the list, and when a drag hovers over a row, I'll pick the target folder from that row if it's a directory or "..", otherwise use the panel's own folder. To get a drop target for that folder, I'm going to parse its path into a shell item ID first.

Now I'm working out how the drop target gets its shell object: I'll bind the parent folder with SHBindToParent and call GetUIObjectOf on the child to get an IDropTarget, which for a drive root gives the "This PC" folder with "C:" as the child. When the target folder changes, I'll send DragLeave to the old target and DragEnter to the new one, forwarding the other drag calls along the way. I'm also considering IDropTargetHelper so the drag image stays visible over the window, though that's optional and I'll note it for later.

Now I'm wiring up the drop target: when a drag hovers a row, I'll highlight that row and let the shell pick the default effect from the key state, so same-drive drags move and cross-drive drags copy. Dragging onto the same folder is a no-op the shell already handles, and the change notifications refresh both panels after the drop.

Next I'm sketching the file operations worker, starting with a job struct that carries the kind of operation (copy, move, delete, or recycle) and the list of source paths, so F5, F6, and F8 can run through IFileOperation on a background thread.

Still writing the file operation worker: it sets up COM on its thread, creates the IFileOperation object, attaches the owner window and flags, and queues copy, move, or delete calls for each source item.

Still writing the file operation worker: I'm setting the copy flags to allow undo and skip the make-directory prompt, and the delete path will recycle items or delete them permanently depending on the kind of job, with a nuke warning when recycling large items.

Now I'm settling the copy dialog for F5: in Total Commander style it shows the count of selected files with an editable target path, and in Explorer style it's a label with the other panel's folder prefilled. A single item gets its own wording, and Shift+F5 instead prefills just the name so the copy lands in the same folder under a new name.

Now I'm settling how the copy target gets parsed: I'll trim it and resolve relative paths against the source folder. If it ends in a backslash or is an existing directory, it's the destination with no new name. For a single item with a file-like path, I'll split out the parent folder and the new name, creating the parent if needed; otherwise the target becomes a new folder.

Now I'm setting up the input dialogs with a small template builder that lays out a plain dialog box with a title, font, and fixed position and size.

Now I'm laying out the input dialog template by hand: a plain header with style, extended style, and item count, then the dialog's position, size, title and font, followed by each control's class and placement.

Still writing the dialog template code: the listview class and item IDs are set up, and I'm now planning the input dialog for things like F7, the copy and move target, and the mask prompts. A confirmation will use a plain Yes/No message box.

Now I'm sketching the search dialog for Alt+F7: a file mask field, a starting path defaulting to the current folder, and a field for text to find inside files. I'm also thinking about whether to add a case-sensitivity checkbox, but I'll leave that out for now.

Now I'm sketching the search dialog's status line and results list, with the search running on a worker thread that can be stopped and reports progress through a timer.

Now I'm settling the search results: when the dialog closes mid-search, I'll set the stop flag and wait on the worker thread, which is safe since it only posts messages. Choosing a result will hand back its path so the active panel can jump to that folder and focus the file. For the viewer, I'm planning a window class with a child edit control that loads up to 32 MB, converts bare line feeds to CRLF, and swaps nulls for spaces.

Now I'm settling the viewer's keys: Esc, F3, F10 or Q will close it, and A, S, U and W will switch encoding or toggle wrapping, since the edit control is read-only and the letters are free. For find, F7 or Ctrl+F will open a simple input prompt and search forward from the current position, ignoring case, over the decoded text I've kept in memory.

Now I'm setting up the layout for the main window: the toolbar height comes from its autosize, and everything else gets scaled to the DPI.

Now I'm laying out the panel internals: a drive bar about 22 to 26 pixels tall with the label to its right, and a tab strip whose height I still need to work out.

Now I'm settling the tab strip height for each panel: I'll ask the tab control to compute its header size and then show only that strip, leaving the file list below it. I'm also setting it to keep focus on the list and to scroll rather than wrap when there are too many tabs.

Now I'm setting the status bar at the bottom of each panel to about font height plus six pixels, and deciding the path header should show a blue-ish background when the panel is active.

Now I'm settling on the header colors: the active panel uses the system active caption color and the inactive one uses the inactive caption color, with the drive letter shown in lowercase.

Now I'm deciding the cursor highlight for the list: the active panel's ".." row gets a light blue background, and the inactive panel just gets a dotted focus rectangle. Marked files will show their text in red.

Now I'm settling how the command-line label gets drawn: the current path followed by ">", right-aligned, and when the text is too wide I'll cut it from the left so the end of the path stays visible.

Now I'm planning the function-key bar at the bottom: flat labels for F3 through F8 plus Alt+F4, each drawn with a separator line, and I'm leaning toward owner-drawn buttons so they match the look of the original.

Now I'm wrapping up the toolbar: I'll use a flat toolbar with tooltips, and set the button text so it shows up as the tooltip instead of a separate label.

Now I'm sorting out the drive bar: the drive buttons will be narrow and show their letters, and the free-space label goes to the right of them.

Now I'm adding the drive toolbar's label after the buttons, plus the "\" and ".." buttons with no icons, and then turning to how the config file gets saved: window position and split, per-panel tabs and sort order, column widths, and general settings.

Still writing the key handler: I'm mapping the remaining keys, with Delete and Page Up/Down getting their own shortcuts, Ctrl+Page Up going up a directory, and Ctrl+Page Down opening the cursor entry.

Still writing the key handler: I'm mapping the left and right arrows, with Alt going back or forward in history and Ctrl opening the entry in the matching panel, and checking the Down and Up arrows for their own Alt and Ctrl shortcuts.

Still writing the key handler: I'm mapping the Ctrl-plus-letter shortcuts, with A selecting all, C, X, and V running copy, cut, and paste, and D opening the hotlist.

Still writing the Ctrl-plus-letter shortcuts: I'm handling P to copy the current path to the command line, R to refresh, T for a new tab, W to close it, and U to swap the panels.

Still writing the Alt-key quick search and the Enter key handling for the command-line-only shortcuts.

Still writing the key handler's command-line branch: I'm checking whether the combo dropdown is open so Enter selects an item there, then clearing the command line and returning focus to the active panel on Escape, and moving focus back to the list on Tab. After that I'm routing the F-keys to the list handler, and about to write the function that runs the command line and saves it to history.

Still writing the command-line parser: I'm handling the cd command, which takes an argument or a path with a leading backslash, and checking for a bare drive letter like "C:" so it switches to that drive's root.

Still writing the command-line helpers: I'm adding the history entry so that a repeated command moves to the top, capping the list at fifty items, and saving it from the combo box on shutdown. Then I'm appending text to the command line and deleting the last character, and forwarding list character input to the app.

Still wiring the character input: I'm making the list's typed characters feed the command line, skipping control codes, and letting Ctrl+Alt combinations through for AltGr characters. Quick-search keys already swallowed on keydown won't reach this path, and a space typed into a non-empty command line gets appended while an empty one is swallowed.

Still writing the input setup: I'm setting the active panel and then opening the directory under the cursor in the left or right panel on Ctrl+Left or Ctrl+Right, going up a level when the cursor is on the parent entry.

Still writing the settings loader: I'm reading the show-hidden flag, the editor path, and the split position from the config, and about to pull the hotlist entries.

Still writing the settings save: I'm saving the window placement, the active panel, the hidden-files flag, the editor path, the split position, the hotlist, the command history, and the drive paths, and I'll use SetWindowPlacement on startup instead of passing placement to CreateWindow.

Still writing the window placement: I'm applying the saved position with SetWindowPlacement before showing the window, so the workspace coordinates come out right. Then I'm starting the F-key button drawing, filling the background and drawing a sunken edge when the button is pressed.

Still writing the toolbar: I'm adding the F-key button drawing and the button definitions, with each one tied to its image and command.

Still writing the Panel's cursor-open handler: I'm handling the parent entry by going up a level, and building the full path from the current directory for everything else.

Still writing the Panel's navigation helpers: I'm handling Go Up by checking for a root path, otherwise moving to the parent and selecting the child I came from. Go Root jumps to the drive's top level, and I'm working out how UNC paths fit into that.

Still on the panel's navigation: when going back, I'm restoring the cursor to the child folder I came from if the previous path is its parent, otherwise leaving the cursor where it is. Then I'm making Focus set the list control's focus and SetActive repaint the header and list when the panel's active state changes.

Next I'm hooking the list's focus notification so a focused panel becomes the active one. I also see that CalcAllDirSizes would start a separate thread for every directory, which would be too many for a folder with hundreds of subdirectories, so I need to cap that.

Still writing the directory size handling: instead of one thread per directory, I'm running a single detached thread that goes through the list of names in turn and posts a result for each one.

Still writing the status line: I'm summing the selected and total sizes for files and folders, counting marked items, and formatting the result as "selected of total" with the file counts.

Still writing the status line's list loop, and now starting the list's window procedure so typed characters go to the command line.

Next I'm finishing the list's mouse handling, with the subclass procedure taking all the typed characters and the cleanup on destroy.

Still on the list handling: I'm making the list click return without the default handling, so I'm setting focus on the list myself, and working out how Shift-click selects a range from the cursor. Then I'm moving to the tab close subclass and the header's owner-draw colors.

Still writing the header's owner-draw: I'm filling it with the active or inactive caption color, then drawing the current path with "*.*" after it, ellipsized if it's too long. I'm also considering whether the active header should use the highlight color with white text instead.

Still writing the panel layout: I'm settling the header and status label styling, then planning to pass the font height and DPI into the panel so the widths can scale.

Still writing the column sizing: I'm reading the widths of the other three columns and giving the name column whatever space is left, with a minimum of 80 scaled pixels. Since the header's end-of-track notification may fire before the new width is applied, I'm going to respond to the item-changed notification instead, which runs after the change.

Now I'm wiring the list's column and resize handling: the name column takes whatever width is left, and I'm refreshing it after the item count changes so a scrollbar appearing or disappearing doesn't throw the layout off.

Still writing the panel's row drawing: I'm fetching the file entry for this row and its bounds, stretching the bounds to the full list width, and picking the background, using the drop-target color when hovered and the cursor color when this is the cursor row in the active panel.

Still writing the row drawing: I'm switching to cached brushes for the white, cursor, and drop-target backgrounds instead of creating one per row, then setting the text color, marked rows in one color and hidden or system entries in another, and reading each column's width.

Still writing the row drawing: I'm sizing the icon and vertically centering it, then drawing the up-arrow for the parent entry or the file's cached icon otherwise, and setting up the name text rectangle inside the first column.

Still writing the row drawing: I'm drawing the name text into the first column, then the extension in the second, and computing the size string for the third, showing a placeholder for folders whose size isn't known yet.

Still writing the row drawing: I'm drawing the file's size into the third column, right-aligned, with a placeholder for folders whose size isn't known yet. Then the date goes into the last column when the row isn't the parent entry, and a focus rectangle is drawn on the cursor row when the panel is inactive.

Still writing the icon lookup: for directories I'm just using the folder icon and marking it final, and for files I'm getting the icon for the extension and, where that type needs a per-file icon, requesting it once.

Still writing the up-arrow icon for the parent entry: I'm drawing it as a simple polygon sized to the icon, centered in its box.

Still writing the up-arrow icon for the parent entry: I'm drawing the stem and arrowhead as lines inside the icon box, then restoring the old pen.

Still writing the list's custom-draw handling: on each item's prepaint I'm handing the row to my draw routine, and the display-info callback is filling in the text and icon for each column.

Still on the panel's mouse and notification handling: I'm wiring the double-click so an activated row opens the cursor's item, and I'm wondering what a double-click on the empty space below the rows should do.

Still writing the sort handling: a column click toggles direction if it's the same column, otherwise it sets the new column with descending order for the size and date columns. I'm keeping the cursor on the same file name across the re-sort, and the Ctrl+F3-style commands will follow the same toggle rule.

Still writing the drop-target lookup: I'm converting the drop point into list coordinates and hit-testing it, so that dropping on the up-arrow row gives the parent folder, and dropping on another directory row gives that directory's path.

Still writing the drop-target highlight: I'm making sure the row under the cursor is the only one marked, and redrawing the old and new rows so the highlight moves cleanly.

Still writing the drop handling: I'm making the drop target tell the helper to hide its image while the highlighted row changes, then show it again, and tracking the last row so this only happens when it actually moves. Next up is the app's run loop, which waits on the panels' directory-watch handles alongside the message queue.

Still writing the run loop: I'm building the list of directory-watch handles from both panels, waiting on them alongside the message queue, and handing a signaled watch to its panel before draining any pending messages.

Still writing the run loop: the next part handles WM_KEYDOWN-range messages by sending them to the root window first, so the pretranslate hook gets a chance before the message goes to the dialogs and normal dispatch. I'm also checking how WAIT_FAILED should be handled, since an invalid watch handle could otherwise make the loop spin.

Still on the run loop: when a directory watch fires I hand it to its panel, and if the wait comes back as a failure I'll add a short sleep so an invalid handle can't spin the CPU. Panels rebuild their handles each pass, so closing one during navigation is safe.

Still on the run loop: the window-message dispatch can't just send a custom WM_APP+1 to whatever the root window is, since shell property sheets in this process might give that number their own meaning. I'm looking at a registered message name or checking that the root is our own app window before sending the pretranslate call.

Still writing the run loop's message handling: I'm checking for the pretranslate hook with a registered window message instead of WM_APP, so a shell property sheet in this process can't misread it. Next is the Properties command on the active panel, collecting the selected names.

Still writing the Properties and clipboard helpers: for Properties I'm showing the folder's properties if nothing is selected, otherwise invoking the shell's properties verb on the selection. Next, the copy-names command builds the selected names into one string, joined with line breaks, as full paths or bare names, and sends it to the clipboard.

Still writing the About dialog's text: I'm reading the process's current and private memory figures and putting them into the version string shown to the user.

Still writing the MKDIR command: I'm taking the cursor's name as the default, unless it's the parent entry, and then asking the user for the new directory name.

Still writing the MKDIR command: I'm normalizing the typed name against the panel's path and creating the directory with the shell helper, which handles multi-level paths. If it already exists, I'll show a message instead of failing silently, and otherwise report the error text.

Still writing the delete confirmation: I'm building the description of what's being deleted, quoting the name for a single item and otherwise counting the items with the right plural form, then choosing between the permanent-delete and recycle-bin prompts.

Next I'm setting the fallback starting paths for the two panels: the left one defaults to C:\, while the right one uses D:\ if that drive exists, and otherwise the user's profile folder.

I also want to handle command-line arguments, so that /L= and /R= set each panel's folder after loading, and a bare path argument opens in the active panel.

Still writing the app.rc resource script: I'm wiring up the icon, the manifest, and the version info block.

Still writing the app.rc version info block, filling in the company, description, file version, and product name strings.

Still writing the manifest: I'm setting up the XML assembly identity and the common-controls dependency so the window gets modern visual styles.

Still writing the manifest: I'm adding the DPI-awareness settings inside the windowsSettings block.

Still writing the manifest's windowsSettings: I'm declaring per-monitor DPI awareness and long-path support, then closing out the trust info section.

Still writing the CMake setup: I'm declaring the project as C++20 with extensions off and defaulting to a Release build when none is chosen, then adding the WIN32 executable target.

Still writing the CMake target: I'm listing the remaining source files for the executable and adding the Windows-specific compile definitions for Unicode, strict types, and the target Windows version.

Still writing the CMake target: I'm wiring the version string into the compile definitions and the Windows link libraries, with MSVC-specific flags to avoid a duplicate manifest.

Still writing the CMake link setup: for MSVC I'm adding warning and UTF-8 flags and disabling the automatic manifest so it doesn't clash with the embedded one, and for MinGW I'm linking statically with the wide-character entry point.

Still writing the CMake presets: I'm adding the first configure preset.

Still writing the CMake presets: I'm adding the MinGW release preset with Ninja, pointing at g++ and windres, and then a MinGW debug preset and an MSVC preset.

Still writing the CMake presets: I'm setting the Russian-comment convention for the project code and laying out the VS Code settings, launch, and task files.

Now I'm drafting the icon with Pillow: a 256 by 256 image with a dark blue rounded background, two light panels, blue header bars, and a yellow folder accent, saved as an ICO across the common sizes.

Still writing the shared header: I'm including the Windows, common-controls, and shell headers, then defining the global instance handle and the custom app message IDs, starting with the icon-loading message.

Still writing the shared header: I'm defining the common message IDs for icon loading, directory sizing, operation completion, search completion, and closing the inline edit field, then starting the ComPtr smart-pointer wrapper.

Still writing the ComPtr move and access helpers: I'm adding move assignment, dereferencing, a bool check, and methods to reset the pointer or take a reference from a raw pointer.

Still writing the Scale helper: I'm converting a value to the current DPI using MulDiv against the 96 DPI baseline.

content.text:
I'm going to write the actual project now, since this is a large task. My plan is a CMake-based layout with presets for Ninja and GCC, VS Code settings, and some documentation files, which I'll build with MinGW.

Still listing the source files for the project: the app entry point, main window, file panel, file system enumeration, formatting, shell integration, a read-only viewer, and input dialogs.

Next I'm planning the dialogs as .rc resources, with a search dialog for Alt+F7 that runs in a worker thread and lists results. Config will go into a portable INI file next to the exe, saving window position, tabs, paths, column widths, and sort order.

I'm working out the toolbar next: standard system bitmaps for the common actions, with buttons for refresh, back and forward, copy, move, new folder, delete, search, properties, a command prompt, and Notepad. Each panel will also get a row of drive buttons plus a line showing the working folder's free space.

I'm laying out the rest of the panel: a row of function-key buttons along the bottom (F3 view through F8 delete, plus Alt+F4 to exit), with a command line above them. Each panel is a virtual-mode ListView in report style with its own column headers and a status line at the bottom.

I'm settling on the ListView approach: report style with virtual data, so the native header handles sort arrows and column resizing. Since the ListView's own selection can't carry TC's cursor-versus-mark distinction, I'll keep marks in a separate set and color them through custom draw, with the cursor as the single-select highlight.

I'm working out the keyboard and mouse behavior next: Insert toggles the mark on the cursor item and moves down, Space toggles it too, and Num+, Num- and Num* handle selection by mask or inversion. For the mouse, plain clicks move the cursor, Ctrl+click toggles marks, and Shift+click marks a range, which means subclassing the ListView to intercept those clicks before the default selection behavior takes over.

I'm settling the keyboard and mouse handling: the list gets subclassed so Ctrl-click toggles a mark and Shift-click marks a range before default selection kicks in, and keys like Enter, Backspace, Tab, Insert, Space, the function keys and Delete get intercepted first. I'm keeping the native ListView for its header, scrolling and keyboard navigation rather than custom-drawing the whole panel.

Now I'm settling on how keys get routed: rather than handling them one list at a time, I'm planning to check each message in the main loop before translation, sending panel and command-line keys through a single central handler. That approach fits the classic commander layout, where typed letters go to the command line.

I'm wiring the message loop so each key press gets checked before translation, passing it to the app's handler when focus is in the main window and not a dialog. Typed letters in the file list go to the command line instead of moving the cursor, Enter runs the command if there is one and otherwise opens the item, Backspace trims the command line before it goes up a folder, and Esc clears it.

I'm working out how the command line gets run: a "cd" command will just change the panel's folder, and anything else will go to CreateProcess in the panel's current directory, with ShellExecute as the fallback for documents and links.

I'm settling on how the command line runs things: Enter tries ShellExecute on the first token with the rest as parameters, falling back to a cmd window if that fails, and Shift+Enter goes straight to cmd so the window stays open. The command history will live in a dropdown combo and be saved to the INI file. For the path header, I'm leaning toward a simple static control with ellipsis truncation rather than a custom-painted child.

I'm settling the path header now: the active panel's header gets a blue background with white text, and a click just activates the panel. A double-click will open an in-place edit over the header that navigates on Enter and tears down on Escape or focus loss. Next to it go a hotlist button bound to Ctrl+D and a history dropdown. I'm also starting on the per-panel drive bar, with a button for each drive plus root and parent.

I'm wiring up the per-panel drive bar as a toolbar with the system drive icons, marking the current drive with a check-group button. A static control beside it will show the free space, and I need to rebuild the bar whenever a drive is added or removed.

Now I'm working out the tab strip: labels that show the drive letter and folder name, like "e:gui_project", with double-click or middle-click closing a tab. Ctrl+T opens a new one, Ctrl+W closes it, and Ctrl+Tab switches between them. I'm leaning toward always showing the strip rather than hiding it when there's only one tab, since that keeps the layout simpler.

Now I'm settling the panel's columns: name, type, size and date, with the name shown without its extension and the extension in its own column. Directory rows will show "<Папка>" for size, and the first row will be "..". The date will follow a dd.mm.yy hh:mm pattern, and sizes will switch units dynamically rather than staying fixed to bytes.

Next I'm settling the sort order: directories always come first, sorted by name, and files follow using whichever column was clicked. Name sorting uses natural order, extension sorting falls back to name, and dates and sizes compare directly. Reversing the direction just flips the comparison, and ".." stays pinned at the top. For the icons, I'll pull the shared system image list through SHGetFileInfo so each row shows the right shell icon.

Now I'm planning the icon handling: regular files will take their icon from the system image list by extension and cache it, while executables, shortcuts and similar types get looked up individually in a background thread, and folders just use the generic folder icon.

I'm setting up the icon loader as a single background worker thread that takes requests with a target window, generation, item index and path, so per-file icons for executables don't stall scrolling. Each result gets posted back to the panel with the generation and the item and icon indices packed together.

I'm weighing how to get icon results back to the panel: a heap-allocated result struct posted to the window, or a mutex-guarded queue. The pointer approach is simpler. Since sorting reorders items, I'm now thinking the icon request should refer to a stable entry id rather than the displayed index.

I'm settling the panel's data model: a master list of entries in load order, plus a sorted view of indices into it, with marks and icons stored on each entry. Icon requests will reference the entry's position in the master list, and each reload bumps a generation counter so stale icon results get ignored. I'm also weighing whether a synchronous directory read is fast enough locally, which it likely is, though network folders could stall.

Now I'm setting up the auto-refresh: a change-notification handle on the panel's folder, waited on alongside the other handles in the message loop. When it signals, a short debounce timer will fire and reload the panel while keeping the cursor and marks in place.

Still working out the message loop: waiting on the directory change handles alongside the window messages, and calling back into the app when one fires. Once handled, the notification gets re-armed and the loop carries on. I'm also thinking about the debounce, so a burst of file changes during a copy triggers a single reload.

I'm working out how the file operations will run: copy and move through F5 and F6 with an editable target path, handled by IFileOperation so the native progress and conflict dialogs come for free. The open question is whether calling it straight from the UI thread is safe, since it may pump messages internally.

I'm weighing whether to run the file operation on a background thread so the UI doesn't freeze during the copy, since PerformOperations blocks the caller. Leaning toward a worker thread with the main window as owner, though cross-thread ownership brings its own input-queue concerns I still need to check.

Now I'm settling on the worker-thread route for the copy, and I'll pass the main window as owner so the progress and conflict dialogs stay attached to it. Once the operation finishes, I'll post a completion message so the panels refresh, though the change notifications would catch that anyway. For a copy into a target from the dialog, if the target is an existing folder, I'll call CopyItem with that folder as the destination.

I'm working out the copy target logic: if the destination ends in a backslash or is an existing folder, the files go into it, and for a single file the typed name can rename it on the way. For a missing parent or multiple sources I'll create the folder first. Next I'm settling delete on F8 and Del, with a confirmation prompt and the recycle bin via IFileOperation.

I'm settling the delete behavior now: plain F8/Del sends items to the recycle bin silently through IFileOperation, and Shift+Del skips the bin and the undo option. Renaming on Shift+F6 will use in-place label editing, though I still need to work out how the extension-less display of the name column fits with that.

I'm settling how the rename works: Shift+F6 turns the name into an in-place edit box with the extension left out of the selection, and on finish it moves the file and puts the cursor on the new name. The one thing left to handle is that a plain click on an already-selected item shouldn't start an edit, so I'll cancel that case in the begin-edit handler.

I'm adding a new-folder command on F7 that asks for a name through an input dialog and creates the folder, including any missing parents, then moves the cursor onto it. For F3 I'm building a read-only viewer window around a multiline edit control, loading the file in Consolas and capping how much gets read so large files don't exhaust memory.

I'm settling the viewer's text handling: it detects UTF-8 or UTF-16 from the byte order mark and otherwise falls back to the ANSI code page. I'm also deciding which keys close the window and planning a W toggle for word wrap, though I'm leaving the encoding switch keys and find function for later.

I'm settling the viewer's controls now: A switches to ANSI (CP1251), S to DOS (CP866), and U to UTF-8, with W toggling word wrap and Esc closing the window. For binary content I'll swap NUL bytes for a visible dot so the edit control doesn't stop early, and I'm leaving image preview out of this first version.

I'm handling the viewer's keys through a general pre-translate hook: the message loop finds the root window of whatever has focus and, if that window is a viewer, lets it take the key before the edit control swallows it. The search dialog will stay modal, with its results posted back to the dialog window.

Now I'm planning the F4 edit command: it'll open the file in an editor set in the config, falling back to notepad, via ShellExecute. For Alt+F7 search I'm building a modal dialog with a start point, a file mask (defaulting to *.* and accepting ';' or spaces as separators), and an optional text field, with a results list where double-clicking jumps the panel to the file. A worker thread will walk the folders with FindFirstFileEx and match masks using PathMatchSpec.

I'm working out the text search: it'll look for the needle encoded as UTF-8, CP1251 and UTF-16LE, reading files in chunks. I'm still deciding whether matching should be case-insensitive for ASCII and Cyrillic.

I'm settling the search's case handling: for Cyrillic in the ANSI encoding I'll lowercase both the needle and the buffer through a lookup table, while for UTF-8 I'm only planning ASCII case folding, since full Cyrillic folding there is harder.

I'm settling the UTF-8 case folding for the search: for Cyrillic I'll remap the two-byte sequences in place, moving capital letters to their lowercase forms and leaving the byte count unchanged. Because the length stays the same, I can overlap chunks by needle length minus one and still catch matches that straddle a boundary.

I'm wrapping up the text search design: UTF-16 matching is being skipped for now, and the file reading will use 1 MB blocks with the tail of each block carried into the next. Results will go into a mutex-protected list that the dialog drains with a 100 ms timer, which avoids flooding the message queue. I still need to work out how the right-click context menu gets its shell menu.

I'm now settling the context menu: I'll get the shell's menu for the selected items by binding the folder as an IShellFolder and resolving the child PIDLs. The menu gets built with QueryContextMenu, shown with TrackPopupMenu, and the chosen command is run through InvokeCommand.

I'm wiring up the context menu's remaining pieces: for the background menu on empty space, I'd get the current folder's IShellFolder and ask it for its own IContextMenu, reusing the same tracking code. After that I'm moving on to the Alt+Enter properties command via SHObjectProperties.

Now I'm working out how drag and drop fits in: the file list would start an OLE drag from its selected items, probably through the shell's data object, though I'm leaving that for after the first version.

Now I'm planning drag and drop: the file list will start an OLE drag from the selected items through the shell data object, with a drop target that forwards to the folder's own drop handler. I'll call OleInitialize on the UI thread so RegisterDragDrop works, though the scope is getting large and I'll need to be careful about correctness.

I'm checking which compiler quirks to expect with MinGW, since mingw-w64 does provide IFileOperation and I may need a fallback define for FOFX_RECYCLEONDELETE. I'll confirm the shell and COM headers compile before going further.

I'm settling the project's remaining details now: the window DPI handling, using per-monitor awareness through the manifest, and scaling sizes with the window's current DPI. For fonts, I'll take the system message font, and when the DPI changes I'll rebuild the fonts, relayout, and apply the suggested window rect.

I'm settling the ListView's look now: I'll skip the Explorer theme so the cursor row keeps the classic solid highlight, and paint the focused row in a light blue through custom draw for the active panel.

Now I'm working on the custom draw for the list view: I'll clear the selected and focus states so my own colors show, and paint the cursor row differently when it belongs to the active panel. Marked entries get their own text color.

Next I'm making the ListView draw the cursor row myself: clearing the selected and focus states so my own colors show, painting the cursor in a different shade for the active panel, and keeping selection tied to the cursor row.

I'm checking whether clearing the selected state in custom draw still works once the themed ListView is in use, since I remember comctl v6 may ignore that change. A safer route might be to turn off the visual theme on the list so the classic highlight behaves predictably.

Now I'm weighing whether to disable the list's visual theme or draw every row myself. Owner-drawing the whole row, with icons and each column's text placed by the header widths, gives the most control and should be fast enough.

Now I'm planning to custom-draw each row myself: a background fill, the shell icon placed at the left edge, and each column's text right-aligned or left-aligned within the header widths, with ellipsis for overflow. I'll paint the cursor row's background in its own color and leave the list font as the list already set it.

I'm going to draw the inactive panel's cursor as a dotted focus-style frame, while the active panel gets a filled light blue bar. The "..", the parent-directory row, needs an icon too, and I'm weighing a folder icon against drawing a simple arrow myself, since loading a shell32 icon by index feels unreliable.

Now I'm handling the mouse in the list subclass, starting with the left button: if Ctrl is held, I toggle the mark on the item under the cursor, move the cursor there, and skip the default handling so no drag begins.

Now I'm handling the mouse and keyboard in the list: a Shift-click marks the range from the cursor to the clicked row, a right-click opens the context menu through WM_CONTEXTMENU, and receiving focus makes that panel the active one.

I'm mapping out the keyboard handling for the panels: Tab switches panels, Enter runs the command line if it has text or otherwise opens the cursor item, and Backspace either edits the command line or goes up a folder. Insert and Space would toggle the mark on the cursor item, and I'm still deciding whether Space should also compute a folder's size.

I'm weighing whether to compute directory sizes in a background thread and post the result back to the panel, with Space marking the item when the command line is empty. For the selection keys I'm planning the numpad shortcuts: Num+ and Num- for group select and unselect, Num* to invert, and Ctrl+A to select all.

Now I'm working through the remaining keyboard shortcuts: F2 or Ctrl+R to refresh, F3 through F8 for the usual file operations, and Delete when the command line is empty. Shift+F5 would copy within the same panel with the name prefilled, Alt+F1 and Alt+F2 open a drive menu for each panel, and Alt+F7 starts a search.

I'm mapping the remaining shortcuts: Alt+Left and Alt+Right for history, Alt+Down for the history dropdown, and Ctrl+D for the hotlist. Tabs get Ctrl+T to open and Ctrl+W to close, with Ctrl+Tab cycling between them, while Ctrl+U swaps the panels. For sorting, Ctrl+F3 through Ctrl+F6 map to name, extension, date, and size, and Ctrl+H toggles hidden files.

I'm going to handle the remaining keys in the list: Esc clears the command line, and typing letters feeds the command line. I'm weighing a quick-search feature on Alt+letters, though that may clash with menu mnemonics, so I'm leaning toward a Ctrl+Alt variant instead.

I'm now planning the quick search feature: Ctrl+Alt plus a letter opens a small floating edit at the bottom of the panel that moves the cursor to the first prefix match, closing on Esc or Enter. I'm leaning toward keeping that version basic, since the project is already large, and then I'll move on to laying out the menu command IDs.

I'm settling on building the menus and dialogs in code rather than through a resource file, since that avoids codepage problems with the Russian text. Dialogs will be assembled as an in-memory template through a small helper class.

I'm settling on a small in-memory dialog template builder for the dialogs, so they get native Tab and Enter/Esc handling. The resource file will only carry the icon, manifest, and version info, with ASCII strings there.

Writing CMake config with compile definitions and warning flags...

Writing CMake link settings and compile flags for the MinGW build...

Now I'm settling on Win32 threads with CreateThread and an SRWLOCK wrapper instead of std::thread or std::mutex, since the MinGW thread model may not support them reliably. Executable size should stay small with static linking and -Os.

Now I'm settling the config file: it goes next to the executable if that folder is writable, otherwise under the user's AppData. The saved state covers window placement, both panels' tabs and active tab, sort settings, column widths, the hidden-files toggle, command history, the hotlist, and the editor path. Then I'll turn to the per-panel drive toolbar, which needs the shared system image list set up.

Now I'm setting up the toolbar for the drive buttons: each one shows a short text label beside its icon, using the shared system image list, and I'm working out the list-style and mixed-button flags needed to make the labels appear.
